papers.abstract: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC). Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies. From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months. IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.

papers.abstract: Somatic variant detection is technically challenging due to low variant allele fractions, the confounding presence of germline variation, and reference bias. Linear references, such as GRCh38, miss sample-specific variation, leading to misalignments and incorrect variant calls. Although telomere-to-telomere donor-specific assemblies (DSAs) accurately represent individual genomes, their application is limited by cost and technical barriers. Alternatively, the graph-based human pangenome provides a scalable framework to improve read alignment and perform genome inference. Here, we benchmarked somatic variant detection using GRCh38, graph-based pangenomes, and pangenome-inferred DSAs with a HapMap mixture dataset and the COLO829 melanoma cell line. Pangenome-guided alignment improves read mapping and somatic variant calling accuracy. Furthermore, personalized pangenomes partially reconstruct donor-specific genomic content, improving accuracy, reducing germline contamination, and enabling detection of events in loci absent or poorly represented in GRCh38. These findings demonstrate that graph-based and personalized pangenomes are effective strategies for enhancing somatic variant detection compared with GRCh38.

papers.abstract: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) maintains a poor prognosis due to its aggressive behavior and limited therapeutic response. Preclinical progress is severely hindered by traditional subcutaneous models that often fail to metastasize, despite one-third of uLMS patients displaying metastases at diagnosis. This study aimed to establish a reproducible, physiologically accurate orthotopic uLMS murine model that faithfully recapitulates disease progression and chemotherapeutic response. Primary subcutaneous tumors were established via SK-LMS-1 cell injections in NOD/SCID mice. Harvested xenografts were surgically implanted heterotopically (subcutaneous flank) or orthotopically (uterine myometrium). Eight days post-implantation, mice were randomized to receive intraperitoneal doxorubicin (1.2 mg/kg twice weekly) or vehicle control for 3 weeks. Tumor growth was tracked longitudinally via MRI (orthotopic) or caliper measurement (subcutaneous). Immunohistochemistry evaluated tumor vitality, microenvironment hypoxia, vascular density, and metastatic spread. Orthotopic tumors exhibited significantly accelerated growth kinetics compared to subcutaneous counterparts. This expansion was supported by co-option of host uterine vasculature, resulting in ample tumor perfusion, suppressed tissue hypoxia, and robust proliferation. Crucially, 37% of primary orthotopic tumors developed spontaneous, multi-organ metastases to pulmonary, omental, and intraperitoneal sites by 4 weeks. Orthotopic tumors demonstrated heightened sensitivity to doxorubicin, achieving a 55% volume reduction compared to 44% in subcutaneous controls, mediated by superior intratumoral drug delivery supported by increased cleaved caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. Surgical orthotopic xenografting recapitulates clinical uLMS, demonstrating site-dependent vascular co-option, spontaneous systemic metastasis, and enhanced chemosensitivity. By mimicking physiological characteristics of human uLMS, this orthotopic model offers significant potential for enhancing understanding of uLMS and evaluating novel therapies.

papers.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy is a cornerstone of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment, yet resistance remains a significant clinical challenge. Sarcoma antigen 1 (SAGE1), a cancer-testis antigen, has been implicated in various malignancies, but its specific role in TNBC drug response and underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. Using tumor specimens from two prospective TNBC trials, we found that high SAGE1 expression significantly correlates with inferior invasive disease-free survival in patients receiving carboplatin-containing chemotherapy. SAGE1 reduces carboplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo by accelerating DNA damage repair. Mechanistically, SAGE1 enhances global chromatin accessibility and H3K27ac enrichment at Fanconi Anemia (FA) pathway gene loci, interacting with p300 and BRD4 to promote H3K27ac deposition. The BET bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 reversed FA protein upregulation and restored carboplatin sensitivity in SAGE1-enriched cells. Furthermore, SAGE1 interacts with PARP1, and this interaction is associated with the regulation of PARP1 activity and with limited PARP inhibitor sensitivity. Notably, the triple combination of JQ1, carboplatin, and olaparib enhanced DNA damage and suppressed tumor growth in preclinical models. Thus, SAGE1 may contribute to an epigenetic-repair axis by facilitating chromatin opening and bolstering the FA pathway, and targeting this axis via combined carboplatin, PARP, and BET inhibition represents a promising therapeutic strategy for SAGE1-enriched TNBC.

papers.abstract: Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment. Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]). Nine (21%) patients reported 14 treatment-related serious adverse events (alanine aminotransferase increased n=2; febrile neutropenia n=2; pancreatitis n=2; and ascites, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal distension, γ-glutamyltransferase increased, blood alkaline phosphatase increased, cataract, macular oedema, and retinal vein occlusion all n=1). Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation of both nab-paclitaxel and pumitamig in four (10%) patients, discontinuation of nab-paclitaxel only in three (7%) patients, and discontinuation of pumitamig only in two (5%) patients. There were no treatment-related deaths. Treatment with first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel showed encouraging antitumour activity in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and a safety profile consistent with the mode of actions of both agents. These findings warrant further clinical evaluation in global phase 2 and 3 trials. Biotheus (BioNTech group). For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.abstract: Digital health may extend cardiovascular care in communities with limited specialist access, but its effectiveness depends on whether communities have the infrastructure, devices, affordability, and capacity needed to use digital services. We linked national data on cardiometabolic disease burden, cardiology workforce, and digital readiness across 82,999 US census tracts. Among high-burden tracts in counties with no cardiologist or declining per-capita cardiologist supply, 4,765 (18.0%) tracts representing 19.9 million residents had higher digital readiness and were thus classified as deployment-priority tracts, whereas 21,752 (82.0%) tracts representing 74.1 million residents had lower readiness and were investment-priority tracts. Investment-priority tracts were spread across the urban-rural continuum and faced different barriers (adoption versus infrastructure). Contrasting classifications frequently occurred among neighboring census tracts within the same metropolitan area, highlighting geographic variation not captured by county-level targeting. Findings were broadly consistent across nine additional analyses with varying measures of readiness, workforce access, and classification thresholds. These findings provide a national framework for distinguishing communities where digital cardiovascular care may be deployed from those where infrastructure and adoption support may first be needed to enable equitable implementation.

papers.abstract: T cells engineered to express recombinant T cell receptors (TCRs) or chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) can induce durable clinical responses in solid and hematological malignancies. However, manufacturing is resource intensive and often yields highly differentiated, exhausted T cell products. To address this, we developed an antigen-scaffold (Ag-scaffold) technology that presents cognate antigen alongside stimulatory cytokines to preferentially expand genetically engineered T cells. We expanded CRISPR-Cas9- and lentivirally engineered TCR T cells with peptide MHC (pMHC)-presenting Ag-scaffolds and anti-CD19 CAR T cells with CD19-presenting Ag-scaffolds. By applying cognate pMHC Ag-scaffolds, we achieved on average 69% (±22%) antigen-specific T cells after 14 days of culture with a cytotoxic, proliferative profile. Ag-scaffold expansion enhanced initial TCR and CAR cytotoxicity; repeated rechallenges showed sustained control. In vivo, Ag-scaffold-expanded CRISPR-Cas9-engineered NY-ESO-1-specific TCR T cells and anti-CD19 CAR T cells also showed improved tumor control in lymphoma and solid tumor xenograft models compared to cells expanded with IL2/7/15.

papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has emerged as a novel risk factor for pancreatic cancer, particularly early liver metastasis. However, the underlying mechanisms and effective therapeutic strategies remain largely unclear. Here, based on clinical databases, patient tissue samples, and single-cell sequencing of mouse models, we identified CD44 as a key contributor to MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer progression. High CD44 expression was significantly associated with poor survival in patients with pancreatic cancer and was further elevated in MAFLD-associated liver metastatic lesions. Considering that the limited effects of single treatment, we developed a cationic DOTAP/cholesterol liposomal nanoplatform co-loaded with gemcitabine, IR780, and CD44 siRNA (GIR@Lip) for combined chemotherapy, photothermal therapy, and immunotherapy. GIR@Lip nanoparticles exhibited excellent size uniformity, stability, and photothermal conversion efficiency, which could efficiently inhibit KPC cells' viability, migration and invasion, downregulate CD44 expression and stimulate immune response. Furthermore, GIR@Lip efficiently accumulated in tumor tissues in vivo, exhibiting a significant reduction in liver metastatic lesions and remodeling the M1 type tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Collectively, these findings identify CD44 as a potential therapeutic target for MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer liver metastasis and highlight GIR@Lip as a promising multimodal strategy for its treatment.

papers.abstract: Nutrition is a key component of care for critically ill and surgical patients, but the organization of nutritional care and the involvement of dietitians in ICU and perioperative pathways remain variable. This survey aimed to describe respondent-reported nutritional care organization and dietitian involvement among healthcare professionals working in ICU and perioperative settings in France, with a focus on dietitian availability, clinical involvement, nutritional governance, and selected aspects of perioperative care. We conducted a voluntary cross-sectional survey among physicians and dietitians working in French ICU and perioperative settings. The survey was disseminated during the French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine congress, through national professional nutrition and dietetics networks, and via social media. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Overall, 147 professionals responded, mainly ICU physicians and dietitians, and most worked in university hospitals. Among respondents, dietitian availability was reported in 67% of responses, but dedicated time was frequently limited. Involvement was mainly request-based, and participation in medical meetings or ward rounds was uncommon. A medical nutrition lead was identified in 44% of responses, a written nutrition protocol in 50%, and a task-sharing protocol allowing dietitian prescription in 9%. Reported practices suggest that dietitians are available in many French ICUs and contribute to perioperative care pathways. However, access to dietetic expertise does not necessarily translate into dedicated staffing, routine multidisciplinary participation, or structured nutritional governance. Strengthening local organization through medical leadership, written protocols, and multidisciplinary collaboration may help improve the implementation of nutritional care.

papers.abstract: Pulse contour devices estimate cardiac output (CO) from an invasive arterial blood pressure waveform. However, arterial catheters are generally used only in higher-risk patients. By contrast, automatic arm cuff devices are used for noninvasive BP monitoring in almost all hospital patients. Furthermore, these devices measure cuff pressure oscillations, which are directly related to pulsatile blood volume rather than BP. We hypothesised that automatic arm cuff devices can offer an effective means to monitor CO. A custom-built cuff device was used to measure cuff pressure and make a unique measurement of the volume of air pumped into and out of the cuff during linear deflation. Cuff device measurements, an invasive BP waveform from a radial artery catheter, and reference CO from pulmonary artery catheter bolus thermodilution were obtained during interventions from 24 liver transplant and 10 cardiac surgery patients (191 measurement sets). A basic analysis was applied to estimate CO in L min-1 as the product of heart rate, the maximum cuff pressure oscillation amplitude, the cuff-arm system compliance (derived from the cuff pressure-volume relationship), and the body-to-arm surface area ratio (derived from anthropometric information). The arm cuff-based method yielded a correlation of 0.61 (95% confidence interval 0.37-0.79) and a concordance rate of 83% (75%-91%) against the reference CO. For comparison, classic pulse contour analysis of the invasive BP waveform produced a correlation of 0.59 (0.37-0.75) and a concordance rate of 81% (72%-90%). These initial findings suggest potential for convenient CO monitoring using an automatic arm cuff device in surgical patients.

papers.abstract: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is essential for improving survival, but reliance on endoscopy limits feasibility for population-wide screening. We developed ESCCseeker, a minimally invasive risk stratification tool based on peripheral blood mononuclear cells' DNA methylation. In a two-stage multicenter study in China, genome-wide profiling identifies distinct methylation markers between ESCC patients and controls. In the development and verification cohort, machine learning yields a model integrating eight differentially methylated positions with age, gender, SCC-Ag, and CYFRA21-1. ESCCseeker demonstrates robust performance (AUC: 0.987 training, 0.966 test, 0.943 verification), outperforming conventional biomarkers. In a prospective multicenter cohort, the predefined cutoff stratifies individuals into low- and high-risk groups. Restricting endoscopy to high-risk individuals reduces the number of endoscopies needed from 25.02 to 4.78, avoiding 83% of unnecessary procedures while preserving >90% detection sensitivity. These findings establish ESCCseeker as a reliable pre-endoscopic triage tool that minimizes unnecessary invasive procedures and prioritizes high-risk individuals. This trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500095967).

papers.abstract: The first-in-class allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitor asciminib has expanded the therapeutic landscape of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying secondary resistance remain incompletely understood. We investigated clinically observed asciminib resistance mutations by integrating structural modeling, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), quantitative biochemical assays and molecular dynamics simulations. Resistance mutations were grouped into two mechanistically distinct classes: Mutations within the BCR::ABL1 myristate pocket (class I) and mutations located up to 40 Å from the asciminib binding site in the kinase N-lobe, SH2-kinase domain (KD) linker and SH3 domain (class II). HDX-MS demonstrated that asciminib induces conformational stabilization across the KD extending beyond the myristate pocket, establishing a long-range allosteric network. We show that class I mutations reduced asciminib affinity up to 90-fold, consistent with steric interference at the binding site. In contrast, class II mutations retained wildtype binding affinity despite conferring clinical resistance. Instead, the class II mutations F359I and M244V increased intrinsic kinase activity and enhanced BCR::ABL1 autophosphorylation, indicating overactivation. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed allosteric communication linking the myristate and ATP-binding pockets, which is disrupted by class II mutations. Together, these findings establish that asciminib resistance arises through two distinct mechanisms: direct impairment of drug binding or disruption of the asciminib binding-induced autoinhibited conformation. Our study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding resistance to allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitors and has important implications for resistance monitoring, combination therapies and therapeutic sequencing.

papers.abstract: The treatment landscape of ERBB2 (formerly HER2)-positive metastatic breast cancer has evolved substantially during the past decade, with emerging therapies challenging the long-standing induction-maintenance paradigm established by the CLEOPATRA trial (NCT00567190). However, optimal treatment selection, sequencing, and duration remain uncertain, particularly in the context of increasing therapeutic complexity and biologic heterogeneity. Taxane-based chemotherapy combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab has long been the standard first-line induction regimen, followed by maintenance anti-ERBB2 therapy with or without endocrine therapy based on hormone receptor status. Recent data from the DESTINY-Breast09 trial (DB09; NCT04784715) demonstrate superior progression-free survival with trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab, supporting its recent US Food and Drug Administration approval and prompting questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of a dual ERBB2 blockade. Maintenance strategies have also expanded, particularly in hormone receptor-positive disease, with incorporation of endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors, as demonstrated in the PATINA trial (NCT02947685). The HER2CLIMB-05 trial (NCT05132582) provided an additional maintenance approach using a triplet anti-ERBB2 strategy. These nonchemotherapy maintenance options are designed to have fewer toxic effects and better quality of life than chemotherapy-based strategies. These developments raise questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of dual ERBB2 blockade. Emerging biomarker-driven approaches, including the HER2DX assay and circulating tumor DNA, remain investigational and are not yet part of routine clinical practice but aim to optimize treatment selection. Novel strategies, such as chemotherapy-free regimens and sequential multiagent approaches, as in the SAPPHO study (NCT06439693), are challenging traditional paradigms. The management of ERBB2-positive metastatic breast cancer is transitioning toward a more individualized approach that balances efficacy, toxic effects, and patient preferences. Integrating biomarker-driven strategies will be essential to optimize treatment selection, duration, and sequencing, with the goal of improving long-term outcomes while preserving quality of life.

papers.abstract: Professional oncology societies have invested in initiatives to enhance the racial and ethnic representation of the oncology physician workforce, particularly since 2020. Whether these initiatives have contributed to changes in the racial or ethnic representation among oncology trainees and nononcology trainees who provide cancer-related care is unclear. To assess trends in the distribution of underrepresented in medicine (URiM) physician trainees over time across oncology and nononcology specialties, with a focus on trends pre- and post-2020. The URiM category included individuals who identified as American Indian or Alaskan Native; Black or African American; Hispanic, Latino, or of Spanish origin; or Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander race or ethnicity. This repeated cross-sectional study used race and ethnicity data from the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education for trainees in medical, radiation, or surgical oncology; general surgery; and primary care from 2011 to 2025. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to August 2026. The proportion of URiM trainees was calculated by year and specialty. Segmented logistic regression was used to estimate the odds of being URiM overall and by specialty. Overall changes in the likelihood of a trainee being URiM post-2020 (level change) and the annual trend post-2020 (slope change) were estimated. There were 658 891 trainee observations in the cohort, of whom 113 937 trainees (17.3%) were URiM. The percentage of trainees who were URiM was relatively stable from 2011 (5435 trainees [16.1%]) to 2020 (8192 trainees [16.4%]), then increased to 13 345 trainees (20.4%) in 2025. After 2020, there was an overall 5% increase in the likelihood of a trainee being URiM (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.08), as well as a 5% annual increase (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.05-1.06). Within individual specialties, significant post-2020 increases were observed in surgical oncology and general surgery. The post-2020 increase was greatest in radiation oncology (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.11-1.30). This cross-sectional study found that the proportion of trainees who provide cancer care identifying as URiM increased from 2011 to 2025, particularly since 2020; however, URiM representation still did not match the diversity of the general US population in 2025.

papers.abstract: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) comprises a family of rare malignancies subclassified by anatomy and pathology. However, this classification scheme may obscure shared biology and limit patient stratification. Here, we tested whether BTC heterogeneity can be explained by coherent latent axes and evaluated the potential to unify diverse clinical and genomic factors under a tractable biological framework. Whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing was performed on 180 tumors enriched for tumor cells by laser capture microdissection to identify shared programs in BTC. Network integration across transcriptomic classes identified two consensus cancer subtypes (CCS). The CCS segregated with anatomical location of primary tumor, and gene expression marker analyses suggested that subtypes reflect tumor cell of origin differences. The CCS displayed strikingly divergent molecular landscapes, explaining more variance than anatomical location of the primary tumor. CCS-B tumors were mutationally loaded with clock-like and APOBEC signatures and extrachromosomal DNA, whereas CCS-A tumors were characterized by chromosome-arm deletions. This approach showed that harnessing the genomic and transcriptomic diversity of BTC provides insights into shared biology and improves stratification.

papers.abstract: Resistance to targeted therapies is frequently associated with stem-like features and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Understanding whether these programs directly drive resistance or instead reflect increased phenotypic plasticity is needed to guide strategies for overcoming resistance. Here, we found that resistance to ALK inhibitors (ALKi) in non-small cell lung cancer was associated with increased phenotypic plasticity, reflected in enhanced adaptability to orthogonal stressors and increased metastatic potential, without intrinsic cross-resistance in short-term assays. Computational modeling and experimental validation studies showed that plasticity was progressively enriched over multi-step resistance trajectories. Lineage tracing and clonal analyses revealed a substantial, heritable intra-cell line variability in adaptation potential. High adaptation potential was associated with increased chromatin accessibility at EMT/stemness regulators. Adaptation potential could be enhanced by inducing stemness/EMT programs and suppressed by SOX2 knockdown or epigenetic inhibition, with corresponding effects on resistance. Collectively, these findings indicate that targeted therapy indirectly selects for cells with increased phenotypic plasticity, providing a common basis for the resistance-EMT association and the substrate for multifactorial resistance and metastatic competence. Constraining plasticity could delay resistance and extend response durability.

papers.abstract: To identify perioperative factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium (iMg/tMg) ratio at intensive care unit (ICU) admission and on postoperative day (POD) 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. This single-center prospective observational study enrolled adults undergoing elective surgery. Paired iMg and tMg measurements were obtained at ICU admission and on POD 1. The primary analyses evaluated perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio at each time point using univariable linear regression and multivariable linear regression with backward elimination. Exploratory analyses assessed temporal changes using paired t tests. Of 150 enrolled patients, 141 were analyzed. At ICU admission, the ratio was positively associated with iMg immediately after anesthesia induction (P = 0.007) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (P = 0.041), and negatively associated with anesthesia time (P = 0.005) and total cholesterol (P = 0.018). On POD 1, the ratio was positively associated with intraoperative non-Mg-containing fluid volume (P = 0.016), and negatively associated with operation time (P < 0.001), hypertension (P = 0.013), and albumin (P = 0.007). Model R2 values were 0.10 and 0.20 at ICU admission and on POD 1, respectively. In exploratory analyses, the mean ratio increased between postoperative measurements (0.659 to 0.713; P < 0.001). Mean iMg decreased from 0.589 mmol/L after induction to 0.545 at ICU admission, then increased to 0.640 on POD 1 (all P < 0.001). Perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio differed between ICU admission and POD 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. Both models had limited explanatory power. These findings should be interpreted in relation to sampling time and require independent validation before informing clinical management.

papers.abstract: Bispecific antibodies targeting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/PD-1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) pathways represent a promising therapeutic strategy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). HB0025 is a novel bispecific antibody fusion targeting PD-L1 and VEGF. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of HB0025 plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC. This open-label, multicenter, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with stage IIIB/C or IV NSCLC without sensitizing EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations across 13 hospitals in China. Participants included those with nonsquamous NSCLC and squamous NSCLC. Patients were enrolled from January 15, 2024, to May 21, 2025. Data cutoff was April 20, 2026. Patients received intravenous 10-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks or 20-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy: pemetrexed/carboplatin for nonsquamous and paclitaxel/carboplatin for squamous for up to 6 cycles, followed by HB0025 maintenance (with pemetrexed for nonsquamous) until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects. The primary end points were safety and investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, version 1.1. The secondary end points included disease control rate, duration of response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Treatment efficacy was evaluable in 169 enrolled patients. The nonsquamous cohort included 85 patients (median [IQR] age, 63.0 [58.0-68.0] years; 26 [30.6%] female and 59 [69.4%] male patients), and the squamous cohort included 84 patients (median [IQR] age, 65.0 [60.0-69.0] years; 6 [7.1%] female and 78 [92.9%] male patients). In the nonsquamous cohort, confirmed ORR was 36.4% (95% CI, 17.2%-59.3%) and 57.1% (95% CI, 44.1%-69.5%) in the 10-mg/kg and 20-mg/kg dose groups, respectively. In the squamous cohort, ORR reached 68.2% (95% CI, 45.1%-86.1%) and 74.2% (95%, 61.5%-84.5%) at the respective doses. Median PFS was 12.52 months (95% CI, 10.15-16.56) in the nonsquamous cohort and 14.78 months (95% CI, 11.30 to not estimable) in the squamous cohort. The 12-month PFS rates were 54.3% (95% CI, 41.6%-65.3%) and 62.1% (95% CI, 49.9%-72.1%) in the nonsquamous and squamous cohorts, and the 12-month OS rates were 75.8% (95% CI, 65.0%-83.7%) and 85.5% (95% CI, 75.8%-91.5%) , respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 56 of 85 patients (65.9%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 51 of 84 (60.7%) in the squamous cohort, mainly as hematologic toxic effects. Any-grade immune-related adverse events related to HB0025 occurred in 20 patients (23.5%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 21 patients (25%) in the squamous cohort. In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, HB0025 plus chemotherapy showed promising antitumor activity and manageable safety in patients with advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC in both nonsquamous and squamous histologic types, supporting further evaluation in randomized phase 3 clinical trials. papers.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most common form of leukemia in Western countries. The introduction of targeted therapies has expanded first-line treatment options, which differ across multiple relevant dimensions, making therapeutic decisions increasingly challenging. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) was conducted to identify and quantify the importance of key treatment selection criteria and to evaluate available first-line alternatives for patients with mutated and unmutated immunoglobulin heavy-chain variable region (IGHVmut/IGHVunmut) gene status, from the perspective of clinicians, patients, payers, and methodologists. The analysis focused on targeted therapies recommended by European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) guidelines and reimbursed in Italy, including ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, venetoclax + ibrutinib, and venetoclax+obinutuzumab. The MCDA was developed in accordance with International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR) Good Practice recommendations, using the MACBETH (Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical-Based Evaluation Technique) method to elicit stakeholder preferences. Decision criteria were selected based on literature review, stakeholder input, and data availability. Preferences were collected from 20 stakeholders (nine clinicians, five patients, six payers/methodologists) via structured questionnaires. Six criteria were selected: efficacy, safety, quality of life (QoL), drug cost, convenience of administration, and treatment duration. Efficacy and safety emerged among the most important criteria across all groups, with efficacy particularly prioritized in the IGHVunmut population. Among the other criteria, notable differences emerged between stakeholder groups: clinicians assigned relatively greater importance to treatment duration, especially in the IGHVmut population; patients prioritized QoL more than other groups; payers and methodologists gave more weight to drug cost than clinicians and patients. In the IGHVmut population, venetoclax + ibrutinib, and zanubrutinib were the most valued options. In the IGHVunmut population, second-generation Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib) ranked highest. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings. This is the first MCDA study applied to CLL treatment in Italy. It highlights the value of structured, stakeholder-informed approaches in supporting value-based treatment decisions.

papers.abstract: The Central Brain Tumor Registry of the United States (CBTRUS) is the largest population-based site-specific registry in the world and is focused exclusively on primary brain and other central nervous system (CNS) tumors diagnosed in the United States (US). CBTRUS obtained de-identified incidence data from 48 central cancer registries (CCRs) from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's National Program of Cancer Registries and 4 CCRs from the National Cancer Institute's Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program. CBTRUS represents the entire US population and is inclusive of cases of all primary malignant and non-malignant brain and other CNS tumors for 50 state registries, plus the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. Additional survival data from 21 CCRs were obtained from SEER. From 2019-2023, 515,112 tumors were reported, corresponding to an average annual age-adjusted incidence rate (AAAIR) of 27.02 per 100,000 population. Across the 50 states, AAAIR for all primary brain and other CNS tumors varied. Meningioma was the most frequently diagnosed tumor type (43.4%). Females had a higher overall incidence of primary brain and other CNS tumors than males, whereas males had higher incidence of many glioma subtypes, including glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype. Incidence varied by race/Hispanic ethnicity, sex, age, and tumor type. For children 0-14 years of age at diagnosis, primary brain and other CNS tumors were the leading cause of cancer-related mortality which is disproportionate to the AAAIR of these tumors in this age group. For most tumor sites, five-year relative survival generally decreased with older age at diagnosis, with children, adolescents, and young adults generally having better survival outcomes. This report provides a current, comprehensive source for the descriptive epidemiology of all primary brain and other CNS tumors in the United States.

papers.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as important regulators in tumorigenesis through microRNA sponging, protein translation and interaction with RNA-binding proteins. Here, we identified a novel circRNA termed circSMAD4 that was generated by alternative splicing from exon 2 to exon 10 and back to the beginning of exon 2 of SMAD4 pre-mRNA, constituting a 1435-nucleotide circular RNA. circSMAD4 was upregulated in gallbladder cancer (GBC) tissues and positively correlated with cancer progression. Elevated expression and tumorigenic activity of circSMAD4 mainly relied on its interaction with IGF2BP2, where m6A-binding motifs located at KH3 and KH4 of IGF2BP2 recognized and bound to the flanking intron sequences of circSMAD4. In the cytoplasm, IGF2BP2 stabilized circSMAD4 levels, and circSMAD4 in turn inhibited ubiquitination and degradation of IGF2BP2, thereby creating a positive feedback loop for both elevated expressions. Collaboration of circSMAD4 and IGF2BP2 activated JAK2/STAT3 and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signalling. Notably, treatment of xenografted mouse models with CWI1-2, a small molecule for interruption of IGF2BP2 binding to circRNA, resulted in decreases in circSMAD4-induced tumour development. Collectively, our findings suggest that circSMAD4 cooperates with IGF2BP2 to promote tumour progression, highlighting the circSMAD4-IGF2BP2 complex as a potential therapeutic target in GBC.

papers.abstract: Second primary cancer (SPC) risk differs by race and ethnicity among U.S. breast cancer survivors, yet limited data disaggregate Asian American (AA) and Pacific Islander (PI) women. We identified 64,277 AA and 5455 PI women diagnosed with invasive unilateral breast cancer between 2000 and 2019 (followed through 2020) and survived ≥ 1 year in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. We examined SPC risk (all SPCs, non-breast SPCs, and site-specific SPCs) by race (AA, PI) and Asian ethnogeographic regions (East, South, and Southeast). Subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) and cumulative incidence of SPCs were estimated, accounting for competing risks. Over 6.13 median years of follow-up, 4083 AA women (East = 1922; South = 312; Southeast = 1579; Other/Unknown = 270) and 498 PI women developed SPCs. Overall, PI women had higher SPC risk than AA women (SHR = 1.44, 95% CI = 1.31-1.58), driven by contralateral breast, lung/bronchus, ovarian, and digestive system cancers. Among AA women, South AA women had lower SPC risk than East AA women (SHR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.75-0.96), driven by lower lung/bronchus, digestive system, and colorectal cancer risk. Southeast AA women had similar SPC risk to East AA women, but lower digestive system cancer risk (SHR = 0.77, 95% CI = 0.66-0.89), and higher uterine (SHR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.02-1.63) and thyroid cancer risk (SHR = 1.97, 95% CI = 1.47-2.64). One in 10 PI women developed an SPC within 10-years (10.32%) compared with one in 14 AA women (AA = 6.91%; East AA = 7.66%; South AA = 6.25%; Southeast AA = 7.26%). SPC risks were highest among PI breast cancer survivors and differed across Asian ethnogeographic regions. These findings highlight the need to understand factors associated with SPC risks and develop tailored interventions to address these disparities.

papers.abstract: The survival benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) following resection of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) remains controversial; moreover, the patient group that could benefit most from this approach remains undetermined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 423 patients (median age 65 years; 52.2% male; 297 patients who received ACT) who underwent curative intent resection of iCCA between 2021 and 2024. To minimize selection bias, propensity score matching (PSM) at a 2:1 ratio was performed. Overall survival (OS) was the primary end point. Survival analyses were conducted using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression methods. In the PSM-matched cohort, ACT significantly improved OS compared to observation alone (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.52, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.32-0.82, p = 0.005). Subgroup analyses revealed marked heterogeneity in treatment effect. The most remarkable finding was a strong interaction between treatment and histological subtype (p for interaction = 0.041). Patients with small-duct type iCCA derived a substantial survival benefit from ACT (HR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.17-0.63, p = 0.001). In contrast, patients with large-duct type iCCA did not show a significant OS benefit (HR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.45-1.76, p = 0.737). In conclusion, postoperative ACT was associated with improved OS after resection of iCCA. Exploratory interaction analyses suggested that the magnitude of this association may differ according to histological subtype, with a more pronounced survival benefit observed in patients with small-duct type iCCA. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in independent prospective cohorts before histological subtype can be incorporated into treatment-selection strategies.

papers.abstract: To evaluate a histology-derived score (HDS) integrating tumor-stroma ratio (TSR), tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), and tumor budding (TB) for prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer (CRC) and assess its incremental prognostic value. A total of 559 patients with CRC were retrospectively enrolled and randomly split 7:3 into a training cohort (n = 392) and an internal validation cohort (n = 167). TSR, TLS, and TB were assessed on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained sections to construct the HDS, with predefined low- (3-4), intermediate- (5-6), and high-risk (7-8) groups. Independent prognostic factors were identified using multivariable Cox regression and incorporated into a nomogram. The incremental prognostic value of HDS was assessed by comparing nested models using the concordance index (C-index), likelihood-ratio test (LRT), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Multivariable Cox regression identified HDS (HDShigh vs. HDSlow: HR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.75-5.47, p < 0.001), TNM stage (III vs. I: HR = 3.26, 95% CI: 1.49-7.12, p < 0.001), and lymphovascular invasion (LVI) (yes vs. no: HR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.09-2.64, p = 0.020) as independent prognostic factors for disease-free survival (DFS). Adding HDS to TNM + LVI increased the C-index from 0.709 to 0.738 in the training cohort (LRT, p < 0.001; NRI = 0.454, p = 0.012; IDI = 0.050, p < 0.001) and from 0.655 to 0.669 in the internal validation cohort (LRT, p = 0.033; NRI = 0.313, p = 0.148; IDI = 0.029, p = 0.044). The nomogram showed good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility in both cohorts. HDS provided incremental prognostic information beyond TNM stage and LVI in CRC. The HDS-based nomogram may facilitate individualized prognostic assessment, although external multicenter validation is required.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease throughout survivorship. Recent studies documented suboptimal adherence to cardiovascular risk reduction medications, but studies identifying contributors to this behavior are lacking. The association between sociodemographic characteristics, social drivers of health factors, and cost-related medication behaviors in survivors who were taking antihyperlipidemics or antihypertensives was evaluated. These cross-sectional analyses utilized data from the National Institutes of Health All of Us Research Program from May 31, 2017 to October 1, 2023. Cohort eligibility included identifying as Black/African American or White, being at least 18 years old, and having a diagnosis of breast cancer. The outcome, cost-related medication underuse and coping behaviors, was assessed using a seven-item scale. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate the associations of covariates and the outcome for each of the cardiovascular risk medication classes. Compared to Black survivors, White survivors had higher odds of asking for lower-cost medications among antihyperlipidemics users (pooled adjusted OR = 1.69; 95% CI: 1.18-2.40; FDR-adjusted p = 0.012) and antihypertensives users (pooled adjusted OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.50-2.76; FDR-adjusted p = 0.004). Survivors who reported greater social support were less likely to delay filling their prescription to save money when compared to survivors who reported lower social support. Some survivors are more likely to engage in cost-related coping and underuse behaviors than others. Clinicians, including primary care providers, should include discussions and resources about non-cancer therapy adherence-related financial challenges with their patients who are cancer survivors.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) carries a poor prognosis despite curative-intent resection and adjuvant therapy. Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (Gem-NAP) has become a standard adjuvant regimen for PDAC, yet recurrence rates remain high. This study aimed to identify clinical and pathological factors associated with recurrence and survival in patients receiving adjuvant Gem-NAP following PDAC resection. We retrospectively identified 210 patients with resected PDAC who received adjuvant gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel at a single institution between May 2017 and October 2024. Clinicopathological characteristics, recurrence patterns, disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate models were utilized to identify independent predictors of recurrence and survival. In total, 132 patients (62.9%) experienced recurrence, with a median DFS of 21.0 months (95% CI: 16.7-25.3) and a median OS of 39.0 months (95% CI: 32.7-45.3). Local recurrence (28.6%) and liver metastasis (24.8%) were the most common recurrence sites. Multivariable analysis revealed that preoperative CA19-9 > 37 U/mL (OR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.19-4.34; p = 0.01) and a lymph node ratio (LNR) > 0.14 (OR: 2.98; 95% CI: 1.19-7.47; p = 0.02) were significantly associated with recurrence. Independent predictors of worse DFS included elevated preoperative CA19-9 (> 37 U/mL) (HR: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.04-2.43; p = 0.03), LNR > 0.14 (HR: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.23-2.89; p 0.14 (HR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.11-2.80; p = 0.02). Recurrence after adjuvant gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in patients with resected pancreatic cancer remains common. A high lymph node ratio, R1 resection, and lymphovascular invasion were powerful independent predictors of both poor DFS and OS.

papers.abstract: MLN-Eo (Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia) harboring FLT3 rearrangement is an extremely rare hematologic malignancy for which standardized treatment guidelines are currently lacking. This systematic review synthesizes the largest cohort (39 cases) to date of FLT3-rearranged MLN-Eo. The available evidence supports the role of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the cornerstone for achieving long-term survival and as a potentially curative intervention under current treatment modalities. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) can be used as bridging therapy to transplantation by inducing remission and reducing tumor burden. For patients ineligible for HSCT, TKI-based regimens (combined with chemotherapy) are recommended for disease control, while chemotherapy alone is strongly discouraged due to uniformly poor outcomes. These findings provide a practical treatment framework based on the currently available evidence and may help inform clinical decision-making for this rare and challenging disease.

papers.abstract: The interaction mechanism between autophagy and ferroptosis in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unclear. We identified FSP1 as a core molecular node linking these two critical processes. Mechanistically, the degradation of FSP1 is coordinately regulated by NBR1-mediated autophagic flux and RNFT1-driven K63-linked ubiquitination, collectively exacerbating ferroptosis and PAH progression. Combination therapy involving FSP1 overexpression and the autophagy inhibitor Apelin-13 synergistically alleviates PAH in rats by stabilizing FSP1 and suppressing ferroptosis. This study not only reveals a dual-pathway mechanism regulating FSP1 stability and validates a novel therapeutic strategy targeting FSP1 degradation but also provides a novel combined intervention strategy for the clinical treatment of PAH. The interaction between autophagy and ferroptosis in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains poorly understood. This study aims to elucidate the role of ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) as a central molecular node linking these processes and to explore a combined therapeutic strategy targeting FSP1 degradation for PAH intervention. Molecular biology techniques were employed to analyse FSP1 degradation pathways, focusing on NBR1-mediated autophagic flux and RNFT1-driven K63-linked ubiquitination. A rat PAH model was established to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of combining FSP1 overexpression with the autophagy inhibitor Apelin-13. FSP1 stability was coordinately regulated by autophagy and ubiquitination: NBR1 promoted autophagic degradation of FSP1, while RNFT1 exacerbated this process via K63-linked ubiquitination, collectively accelerating ferroptosis and PAH progression. The combination of FSP1 overexpression and Apelin-13 synergistically stabilized FSP1, suppressed ferroptosis, and alleviated PAH symptoms in rats. This study reveals a dual-pathway mechanism governing FSP1 stability through autophagy-ubiquitination crosstalk, highlighting its critical role in ferroptosis-driven PAH. The combination therapy targeting FSP1 degradation presents a novel strategic approach for clinical PAH treatment.

papers.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are stable, evolutionarily conserved non-coding RNAs with covalently closed-loop structures, which function as oncogenes or tumor suppressors to regulate cancer cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and apoptosis. This study explored the role and regulatory mechanism of hsa_circ_0000247 in breast cancer. The expression levels of hsa_circ_0000247, hsa-let-7i-5p, and HMGA1 were detected by RT-qPCR and western blotting. Biological functions were evaluated using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, Transwell, flow cytometry, and electron microscopy assays. The interactions among hsa_circ_0000247, hsa-let-7i-5p, and HMGA1 were verified by dual-luciferase reporter assays, and rescue experiments were conducted. Hsa_circ_0000247 was significantly upregulated in 30 pairs of breast cancer tissues and MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, and BT-474 cell lines. Knockdown of hsa_circ_0000247 inhibited cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and promoted apoptosis. Mechanistically, hsa_circ_0000247 directly sponged hsa-let-7i-5p, which targeted the 3'UTR of HMGA1. Inhibition of hsa-let-7i-5p reversed the effects of hsa_circ_0000247 silencing. In conclusion, hsa_circ_0000247 is upregulated in breast cancer and promotes malignant progression via the hsa_circ_0000247/hsa-let-7i-5p/HMGA1 axis, providing a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target for breast cancer.

papers.abstract: FLASH radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) has garnered significant attention for its "FLASH effect", which selectively protects normal tissues while maintaining tumor-killing efficacy at ultra-high dose rates (UHDR). This technology represents a promising but still investigational therapeutic strategy in radiation oncology. Since the initial confirmation of the FLASH effect in mouse experiments in 2014, related research has rapidly advanced in key radiation physics parameters, radiation types, and biological mechanisms. However, a lack of consensus on its critical triggering conditions, tissue-specific thresholds, and standardized parameters has hindered its transition from laboratory to clinical application. This review systematically outlines the physical triggering conditions of the FLASH effect, revealing its dependence on a multidimensional combination of parameters including dose rate, single-fraction dose, pulse time structure, and radiation type. It also delves into the underlying multiscale biological mechanisms, encompassing radiochemical aspects such as transient oxygen depletion and free radical kinetics, cellular processes including DNA damage repair and cell death patterns, and systemic changes like immune microenvironment remodeling. It further examines three core challenges hindering FLASH-RT's clinical implementation: technical feasibility and equipment limitations, the complexity and uncertainty of biological mechanisms, and challenges in clinical practice and standardization. This review aims to dissect current research progress and critical issues, providing guidance for advancing FLASH-RT's clinical application.

papers.abstract: Intracranial germinomas are highly radiosensitive tumors associated with excellent long-term outcomes. Whole-ventricle irradiation (WVI) with a tumor-bed boost, with or without chemotherapy, has become a standard treatment for localized disease, balancing disease control with reduced treatment-related toxicity. This retrospective study included patients with pure intracranial germinoma treated at Children's Cancer Hospital Egypt (CCHE) between 2008 and 2024. Patients received WVI to 23.4 Gy followed by a tumor-bed boost up to a total dose of 45 Gy. The objectives were to characterize relapse patterns and describe survival outcomes. A total of 63 patients met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Median follow-up was 62.9 months. Six patients (9.5%) developed recurrent disease. Recurrence patterns included one accompanying local pineal and spinal recurrence, one ventricular recurrence, and five cases of distant neuraxial dissemination involving spinal and/or cranial leptomeningeal disease. The local, ventricular, and distant failure rates were 1.6%, 1.6%, and 7.9%, respectively. Overall, intracranial recurrence occurred in two patients (3.2%), whereas distant neuraxial dissemination represented the predominant pattern of treatment failure. Among patients who experienced recurrence, four (66.7%) subsequently died. Estimated 7-year overall survival (OS) and event-free survival (EFS) were 86.5% (95% CI, 78.2%-95.7%) and 80.2% (95% CI, 70%-91.9%), respectively. Endocrine late toxicities were the main adverse sequelae. Whole-ventricle irradiation followed by tumor-bed boost provided excellent local and ventricular disease control in patients with intracranial germinoma. Recurrences were predominantly characterized by delayed distant neuraxial dissemination, emphasizing the importance of long-term surveillance despite favorable survival outcomes.

papers.abstract: The extent and direction of the impact of COVID-19 pandemic disruptions on cancer mortality remain unclear. We assessed observed versus expected cancer mortality from 2020 to 2023 across 54 countries in 14 regions, by cancer type. Using WHO Mortality Database, we calculated age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) for adults (≥ 20 years) from all cancers combined and specifically for lung, pancreatic, breast, and leukemia. Expected ASMRs for 2020-2023 were projected from 2015 to 2019 using Estimated Annual Percent Change. Rate ratios (RRs) of observed versus expected ASMRs were stratified by year, age group, cancer type, country, and region. The analysis included over 2.3 million annual cancer deaths across 54 countries. Lung cancer was the leading cause of death in 45 countries. Eastern Europe had the highest mortality in 2020-2023, with Hungary reporting the highest ASMR (222.6/100,000). Overall, observed mortality was lower than expected (RR < 1). Differences were modest in 2020 but widened by 2023. The largest discrepancies were for breast cancer (RR 0.62-1.19) and leukemia (0.67-1.18), while lung (0.87-1.16) and pancreatic cancers (0.91-1.20) showed smaller differences. Regional variation was notable, with Western Asia showing the widest difference from expected. Differences in expected mortality were limited for poor-prognosis cancers, while breast cancer and leukemia were more affected during long-term healthcare disruptions. Regional disparities illustrate the negative impact of compounding crises on cancer mortality and underscore the need for resilient systems to protect cancer care during emergencies.

papers.abstract: Central venous access is indispensable for clinical management of pediatric patients with hematological disorders, including chemotherapy administration, blood product transfusion, and critical rescue. Repeated venipuncture attempts, procedural failure, postoperative catheter malposition, and cannulation-related complications can substantially disrupt subsequent treatment courses and compromise therapeutic efficacy. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of ultrasound-guided brachiocephalic vein (BCV) cannulation, with the goal of optimizing central venous catheterization protocols, reducing procedure-related adverse events, and improving the efficiency and safety of treatment via central venous access in pediatric patients. This retrospective study included 580 children (303 subclavian vein [SCV], 277 BCV) who underwent ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization between January 2021 and December 2024. We compared first-attempt success rate, overall success rate, procedural duration, intraoperative adverse events, postoperative complications, and catheter malposition. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to improve comparability between the groups with respect to measured baseline covariates. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. After IPTW, the BCV approach was associated with a higher first-attempt success rate (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.05-2.81; risk difference [RD] = 0.119, 95% CI: 0.015-0.222) and a higher overall success rate (RD = 0.091, 95% CI: 0.013-0.168). The mean procedural duration was 6 min shorter in the BCV group (95% CI: -9.5 to -2.5). The BCV approach was independently associated with lower odds of intraoperative malposition (OR = 0.096, 95% CI: 0.037-0.249), postoperative malposition (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.16-0.74), and perioperative complications (OR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.08-0.94). Multivariable regression analysis showed that catheterization approach was independently associated with catheter malposition. Compared with SCV, ultrasound-guided BCV cannulation is associated with higher success rates, shorter procedural duration, and fewer malpositions and complications. This technique may offer particular benefits for children with hematological disorders.

papers.abstract: Cigarette smoking is strongly associated with aggressive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms linking smoke exposure to metabolic reprogramming remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated clinical, molecular, and functional analyses to define a smoking-associated metabolic axis in NSCLC. Lung cancer patients with a smoking history exhibited significantly higher tumor 18F-FDG uptake than never-smokers, suggesting an association between smoking exposure and increased tumor metabolic activity. Consistently, chronic exposure of NSCLC cells to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) or its ingredient benzo[α]pyrene (B[α]P) increased glucose uptake, glycolysis, ATP production, and malignant phenotypes, including proliferation, migration, and sphere formation. Mechanistically, GLUT3 protein, but not mRNA, was selectively upregulated in smoke-exposed tumors and cell models, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. We identified miR-146a as a direct suppressor of GLUT3 through binding to its 3'UTR and found that cigarette smoke markedly reduced miR-146a expression. Smoker-derived NSCLC tumors exhibited lower miR-146a expression and higher GLUT3 levels, which were inversely correlated and associated with poor overall survival. Restoration of miR-146a reduced GLUT3 expression, glucose uptake, and tumor cell proliferation, supporting a central role for the miR-146a/GLUT3 axis in smoking-induced metabolic reprogramming. (-)Gallocatechin ((-)GC), a naturally occurring catechin, is further identified as a selective GLUT3 inhibitor and suppressed smoke-induced glucose uptake, tumor progression, and metastasis without detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings identify the miR-146a/GLUT3 axis as a key mechanism underlying smoking-driven metabolic reprogramming and establish GLUT3 as a potential metabolic target in NSCLC and other GLUT3-dependent malignancies.

papers.abstract: Fatigue is a common symptom in cancer patients associated with impaired quality of life (QoL). Little is known about long-term fatigue trajectories in prostate cancer (PCa) patients. Using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Group Core Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30), 1758 men treated with radiotherapy (2014-2016) for non-metastatic PCa prospectively reported fatigue up to five years later. Associations between pre-radiotherapy characteristics and clinically important fatigue (Score: ≥39/100) two years post-radiotherapy were investigated using logistic regression. Fatigue trajectories were explored using latent class growth analysis and multinomial regression. About 35% (608/1758) of patients experienced clinically important fatigue at least once from the start of radiotherapy up to five years later. Two years post-radiotherapy, 14% of patients reported fatigue, which was associated with pre-radiotherapy fatigue level (OR: 8.67), self-reported diabetes (OR: 1.94), BMI (OR: 1.07), and age (OR: 1.03). Long-term fatigue was strongly linked to pain, insomnia, pelvic symptoms, functional impairments, and reduced QoL. Four fatigue trajectories were identified, characterised by low (45%), moderate (42%), elevated and decreasing (8%), and (6%) increasing mean fatigue levels. Diabetes was associated with a 6 percentage point increase in the probability of experiencing an increasing fatigue trajectory. The findings emphasise the need for early identification of PCa patients susceptible to long-term fatigue. PCa patients with elevated pre-radiotherapy fatigue levels and diabetes may require closer monitoring in risk-stratified aftercare programmes.

papers.abstract: Cancer cells proliferate rapidly and require sustained supplies of nutrients and biosynthetic precursors. Lysosomes are more than terminal degradation sites: they recycle amino acids, sugars, lipids, nucleosides and ions, while also coordinating nutrient sensing, organelle communication and immune regulation. Consequently, lysosomal capacity can become selectively advantageous in tumours by linking nutrient salvage with growth control, organelle communication and inflammatory signalling. Enhanced lysosomal function can support tumour growth, invasion and therapy resistance. Here, we review four cancer-relevant dimensions of lysosomal capacity: catabolism and transport; mTORC1- and AMPK-linked nutrient sensing; membrane contact sites with the ER, mitochondria, and Golgi; and immune regulation spanning innate and adaptive responses and inflammatory control. These functions are context dependent: lysosomal quality control can restrain tumour initiation, whereas established cancers often exploit increased lysosomal capacity to support proliferation, invasion, metastasis and therapy resistance. Finally, we discuss lysosome-state biomarkers and lysosome-targeted strategies for patient stratification and rational combination therapy.

papers.abstract: The genomic characterization of cancers has considerably advanced research and clinical practice. However, critical gaps remain, including limited knowledge of tumor profiles in rare cancers and populations understudied in genomic research and insufficient integration of genomic, clinical and epidemiologic data. This Perspective highlights the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network, established by the US National Cancer Institute to address knowledge gaps in rare and understudied cancers. PE-CGS comprises five research centers supported by a coordinating center and guided by an external advisory panel. Collaborations across PE-CGS are grounded in shared values of participant-centeredness, engagement, access, collaboration and innovation. Activities emphasize participant engagement throughout the research process, including the return of results and collection of clinical and epidemiologic data alongside paired tumor/germline sequencing. PE-CGS demonstrates how engagement, return of results and comprehensive data collection can be integrated to support participant-centered cancer genomics research and accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.

papers.abstract: Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression1,2, whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient -1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.

papers.abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour1-5. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies, such as anti-PD-1 treatment, have achieved great success in various cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes have major roles in the mechanism of action for ICIs, but numerous other components of the tumor microenvironment also contribute to the effectiveness of immunotherapy. However, little is known about the changes in the tumor microenvironment after ICI therapy, which may sustainably affect tumor progression. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data were collected for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patient samples and analyzed to characterize immune cell alterations within the tumor microenvironment. Three different orthotopic allograft HCC models were established for ICI therapy and microenvironment component detection by using flow cytometry and multiple ELISA assays. Transwell assays were combined with flow cytometry to evaluate neutrophil migration. In vitro coculture systems were employed to investigate communication between different cell types. Multiplex immunochemistry analysis was conducted for human clinical samples to confirm the findings. Our results indicate that neutrophil infiltration was significantly reduced after effective ICI therapy, but not in patients with failed immunotherapy. Mechanistically, we found that effective anti-PD-1 therapy activates T cells, which secrete interferon-γ and other cytokines that act on tumor-associated macrophages. This T cell-macrophage crosstalk suppresses tumor-associated neutrophil-related chemokines secreted by macrophages. Consequently, neutrophil infiltration into the tumor microenvironment is diminished. Our findings show that immunotherapy reinvigorates T cells, but also remodels the myeloid compartment and reduces neutrophil recruitment, potentially alleviating neutrophil-mediated immunosuppression, thereby providing potential myeloid-targeted combinatorial strategies for improving checkpoint blockade responses.

papers.abstract: Resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence, underscoring the need for effective perioperative therapies. This nonrandomized, noncomparative phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant ivonescimab monotherapy (cohort 1) or in combination with chemotherapy (cohort 2), followed by surgery and adjuvant ivonescimab. In cohort 2, the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 70.1% (47/67; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 57.7-80.7); the lower bound of the 80% two-sided CI exceeded the historical control rate of 41% and the primary endpoint was met. The MPR rate in cohort 1 was 60.0% (6/10; 95% CI = 26.2-87.8). Among patients who achieved MPR, 83.3% (5/6) in cohort 1 and 97.9% (46/47) in cohort 2 had residual viable tumor (RVT) of ≤5%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 36.4% (4/11) patients in cohort 1 and 30.4% (24/79) of those in cohort 2, with no grade 3 or higher hemorrhage or treatment-related death. Treatment-related surgery delay occurred in one (1.3%) patient. Surgery-related AEs related to ivonescimab occurred in 10.0% (1/10) and 10.4% (7/67) patients in the two cohorts, respectively, with no grade 3 or higher events reported. These data support perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy as a promising strategy for resectable NSCLC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 .

papers.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a 'hot', yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) individualizes perioperative fluid administration according to dynamic hemodynamic variables, but its implementation remains inconsistent and its impact on patient-centered outcomes is still debated. Decision-support and automated systems have been developed to improve adherence, identify fluid responsiveness more efficiently, and reduce the workload of protocolized hemodynamic management. This structured narrative review summarizes the evidence across four outcome levels: process, surrogate hemodynamic, intermediate physiological, and patient-centered clinical. The most consistent evidence concerns process improvement: decision support increases protocol adherence and improves the proportion of fluid challenges that achieve a predefined stroke volume response, largely on non-randomized evidence. Improvements in surrogate hemodynamic control have also been reported, and selected randomized trials suggest favorable effects on microcirculatory flow and lactate. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical benefit. Fluid responsiveness does not necessarily indicate a need for fluid administration, and most available studies remain small, single-center, or focused on surrogate outcomes. Evidence that these systems improve postoperative complications, acute kidney injury, length of stay, or mortality is currently lacking. Ongoing multicenter trials should address this gap. Decision support appears to improve how perioperative fluids are administered, but whether it improves what ultimately happens to patients remains unresolved.
