papers.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival1. Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF-VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells2,3. The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported4,5. Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe-HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2KO) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1-4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5-9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

papers.abstract: Long-term cancer survivors constitute a growing population with characteristic health care needs. Survey-based studies are essential to understanding this population, yet low participation raises questions about potential non-response bias. This study analysed response and non-response in a registry-based cross-sectional survey among long-term cancer survivors in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. A sample of 24 291 adult long-term cancer survivors was drawn from the North Rhine-Westphalian Cancer Registry (diagnosed between 2008 - 2018, ≥5 years post-diagnosis, aged 18-74 at diagnosis). Survivors were contacted by postal letters and asked for consent. Those consenting received a questionnaire. Survey participation was defined as returning a questionnaire (paper-based or online). Age, sex and clinical data (calendar period of diagnosis, tumour stage and ICD-10 group) were available for all invitees and used to compare responders with non-responders. Of 24 291 invited survivors, 3 297 (13.6%) consented and 2 355 (9.7%) answered the questionnaire; 71.4% of those who consented participated. The contact proportion (survivors reached) was 85.8%, and the cooperation proportion (participants among eligible survivors reached) 11.3%. Non-response patterns differed across subgroups: younger survivors were more difficult to contact, whereas older survivors were more likely to refuse participation. Contactability decreased with increasing time since diagnosis. Lower response was observed among survivors with advanced tumour stage and lung cancer, while higher consent was seen among prostate cancer and leukemia survivors. Among consenting survivors, non-participation was mainly due to non-return of the questionnaire, with reported reasons including fatigue and lack of time. Overall response in this registry-based survey was low and primarily driven by non-consent, whereas participation among those who consented was high. In the two-step recruitment approach used in this study, selection occurred mainly at the initial consent stage, while loss after consent was comparatively limited. Future studies using similar procedures should consider strategies to reduce barriers at the consent stage and account for differential response.

papers.abstract: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) is the predominant histologic subtype of esophageal cancer in Western countries and has a poor prognosis. Cytoskeleton-associated protein 4 (CKAP4), a transmembrane receptor involved in proliferation, migration, and signaling, has been implicated in several cancers, but its role in EAC remains unclear. We investigated CKAP4 expression and cellular changes associated with CKAP4 depletion in EAC cell models. CKAP4 expression was characterized using an in vitro Barrett's esophagus (BE) model of EAC progression. CKAP4 was silenced by siRNA in OE33 and OE19 EAC cells. Functional and molecular effects were assessed, and transcriptional changes were analyzed by RNA sequencing. CKAP4 expression varied across Barrett's neoplastic progression, with highest total expression in dysplastic cells and marked surface overexpression in OE33, OE19, and FLO-1 EAC cells. CKAP4 depletion reduced CKAP4 mRNA and protein, altered cell morphology, decreased viability and proliferation, and increased apoptosis. AKT phosphorylation was reduced in OE19 cells and MAPK phosphorylation in OE33 cells, whereas ß-catenin and GSK3ß activity remained unchanged. CKAP4 silencing increased surface expression of adhesion molecules, including integrins α5/ß1 in OE33 cells. RNA sequencing identified >500 differentially expressed genes enriched in immune-related pathways, indicating immune-related transcriptional changes. CKAP4 is a functionally relevant, surface-overexpressed protein in Barrett's-associated EAC. These findings define cellular and transcriptional changes associated with CKAP4 depletion in EAC cells in vitro and support further mechanistic and preclinical investigation; therapeutic and biomarker relevance in EAC remains to be established.

papers.abstract: This study evaluates the statistical robustness of the ISAP cutoff proposed by the 2025 guidelines, re-assesses traditional pathological prognostic factors, and identifies candidates for therapeutic de-escalation regarding chemotherapy omission and fertility-sparing surgery (FSS). We harmonized an institutional cohort (2015-2021, N = 36) with a systematic literature review (1990-2021, N = 193). Missing data were handled via multiple imputation. The optimal ISAP cutoff was determined using AIC/BIC; prognostic factors were evaluated via multivariate Cox regression. Among 229 patients (50 [21.8%] undergoing FSS), ISAP ≥48 months emerged as the optimal cutoff, stratifying 174 low-risk (ISAP <48 months) and 31 high-risk patients. ISAP ≥48 months independently predicted progression-free survival (HR 14.92, 95% CI 3.68-60.38; P < 0.001) and overall survival (HR 20.90, 95% CI 2.22-196.73; P = 0.008). Pathological risk factors showed no prognostic significance. Among low-risk patients managed without chemotherapy, no progression or mortality events occurred (0/85). Four (8.0%) FSS patients required salvage hysterectomy; all achieved 100% survival and none required completion hysterectomy after childbearing. ISAP ≥48 months is a robust prognostic determinant in Stage I PSTT. Surgery alone achieved excellent outcomes in low-risk patients; prospective trials should confirm whether chemotherapy can be safely omitted. FSS is viable for strictly selected low-risk candidates, with salvage hysterectomy providing effective control and subsequent term pregnancies documented.

papers.abstract: MYCN is a member of the MYC family of transcription factors and a potent oncogenic driver across neural crest, neuroectodermal, and neuroendocrine malignancies, including neuroblastoma, where MYCN amplification remains one of the most powerful molecular predictors of treatment failure and poor survival. MYCN has long been considered an ideal therapeutic target, given its restricted expression in postnatal tissues and potent oncogenic activity. However, direct and selective MYCN targeting therapies have yet to be established and translated into the clinic. This reflects the challenges of drugging MYC family proteins, which lack enzymatic active sites and defined binding pockets targeted by conventional small molecules. Here, we examine the landscape of MYCN targeting strategies, from direct approaches such as MYC-MAX dimerization inhibitors to indirect approaches targeting MYCN expression, its interactors, and downstream oncogenic dependencies. We also highlight the potential of targeted protein degrader technology for directly and selectively depleting MYCN protein. We further discuss the profound immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment characteristic of MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma and the therapeutic vulnerabilities this creates. Together, these advances in understanding and technology present a renewed opportunity to translate four decades of MYCN biology into effective therapies to improve outcomes for patients with neuroblastoma and other MYCN-driven cancers.

papers.abstract: Cancer is now one of the defining health and development challenges of our time. The 56 nations of the Commonwealth, home to 2·7 billion people, mirror this global burden. Recorded cancer cases across member states rose by 35% in 2008-18 and the number of deaths reached almost 1·7 million in 2018. The Lancet Oncology Commission on cancer in the Commonwealth was convened to ask a deceptively simple question: how can 56 diverse nations act collectively to close the widening gap between the burden of cancer and the capacity of each country to respond? 80 researchers, clinicians, policy makers, and civil society members, organised into five working groups and ten research streams, spent 2 years assembling the evidence base for this report. Using a validated microsimulation model, we estimate that 5-year net survival across eleven common cancers in the Commonwealth stood at just 30·7% in 2020, ranging from 4·1% in low-income countries (LICs) to 59·0% in high-income countries (HICs), driven overwhelmingly by late-stage presentation, which affects 62% of patients in LICs compared with 43% in HICs. This difference in survival is compounded by chronic underinvestment. Infrastructure gaps are equally stark: only 12% of countries meet international benchmarks for CT imaging, 22% for hospital density, and 40% for radiotherapy. Governance is underdeveloped too: barely one-third of Commonwealth countries have a national cancer control plan meeting basic quality criteria. Research investment also mirrors these inequities: between 2016 and 2023, Commonwealth countries collectively invested only US$165 per cancer-related disability adjusted life year. Yet the case for investment is unambiguous. Our modelling shows that a comprehensive scaleup of treatment, imaging, and quality of care could raise 5-year net survival across the Commonwealth from 30·7% to 52·9%, averting an estimated 5·8 million deaths and adding 113 million life-years between 2025 and 2035, at an incremental cost of $36·7 billion, delivering a return of between four and twenty dollars on every dollar invested. Crucially, this investment need not depend chiefly on external aid, which is contracting sharply at present. Our modelling for 38 low-income and middle-income Commonwealth countries suggests that up to $701 billion in additional domestic fiscal space could be mobilised between 2025 and 2030, through budget reprioritisation, macroeconomic growth, targeted taxation, and prudent borrowing. On this evidence, the Commission proposes six priority actions. These commitments are ambitious, set against an unusually turbulent geopolitical backdrop of declining official development assistance, fiscal retrenchment, and contested multilateralism. Yet it is precisely this backdrop that gives the Commonwealth its distinctive advantage: a voluntary association spanning every income level and continent, bound by common legal and regulatory traditions, capable of collective action that neither purely bilateral aid nor multilateral institutions under strain can easily replicate.

papers.abstract: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) influences the global climate through interconnected atmospheric processes, yet its impact on global and regional temperature-related mortality burden remains unquantified. Here, we integrate global temperature and mortality databases with epidemiological models to assess temperature-related mortality associated with ENSO variability and intensity. During very strong El Niño years, the large amounts of heat released into the atmosphere are associated with an increase in global heat-related mortality of +28.87% (+107,035 annual deaths; 95% eCI: 27,336 to 176,312), and a decrease in global cold-related mortality of -3.70% (-112,681 annual deaths; 95% eCI: -207,619 to -22,203). Increase in heat-related mortality was concentrated in low and medium HDI countries, which accounted for 67.65% of the global increase, with the largest increase in medium HDI countries (+61,863 annual deaths; 95% eCI: 19,939 to 105,888), while point estimates of the combined heat and cold burden suggest a shift of the total burden from high toward lower HDI countries. In a context of continuously warming temperatures, our results indicate that forthcoming El Niño events have the potential to represent new public health challenges, underscoring the need for climate-informed preparedness actions.

papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors are associated with improved responses to immunotherapy. Here, we examined the impact of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s) in TLS formation. Reprogrammed tumor cells into cDC1-like cells remodeled the tumor microenvironment and induced immunogenic TLSs (imgTLSs) across melanoma, colon, bladder, breast, and pancreatic cancer models with distinct genetic backgrounds. cDC1-like cells activated lymphotoxin, TNF, and interferon programs and engaged early with T cells through MHC class I and CD40 signaling to induce imgTLSs containing BCL6+ germinal centers, independently of endogenous cDC1s. Intratumoral positioning shaped distinct cDC1-like cell states, with DC-LAMP+ CCR7+ migratory cDC1s nucleating niches enriched in CD4+, CD8+ T cells, and B cells in mouse and human tumors. ImgTLSs sustained B and T cell responses and promoted systemic immunity through expansion of shared clonotypes in distant, untreated tumors. Our findings outline the spatial organization, signaling programs and interactions of cDC1-like cells that initiate intratumoral lymphoid structures and establish cellular reprogramming as a strategy toward overcoming resistance to immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

papers.abstract: We aimed to explore the effects and mechanisms of MPs on GEC carcinogenesis. Gastric tissues from four adjacent healthy controls and four patients with GC were analyzed for MPs using Raman spectroscopy and Py-GC/MS, alongside proteomic and metabolomic analyses. A series of molecular biology techniques were used for corresponding validation. IHC and IF were used to assess the expression levels of SDHA, EMT-related proteins and CD44 in the gastric tissues of nude mice. Single-cell sequencing was used to examine SDHA and CD44 expression. Eleven types of MPs were identified in both GC and normal control gastric tissue samples. Omics analysis identified SDHA as differentially expressed, with lower expression in GC tissues, while EMT-related proteins and CD44 were increased in GC tissues. PS enhanced GES-1 cell activity and migration, and increased reactive oxygen species levels. After 8 weeks of exposure, focal gastric epithelial dysplasia was observed in PS-exposed mice. PS-fed mice exhibited increased expression of EMT-related proteins and CD44, and decreased SDHA expression in gastric tissues. Single-cell sequencing data were used to observe the possible co-expression of SDHA and CD44 in gastric cells. These findings associate experimental PS exposure with gastric epithelial stress and phenotypic changes and identify SDHA as a candidate metabolic regulator. Further functional studies are needed to determine whether these changes contribute to gastric neoplastic progression.

papers.abstract: Chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard neoadjuvant treatment for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). We previously reported a promising total pathological complete response (tpCR) rate with the de-escalated, platinum-free NeoTENNIS regimen; however, long-term outcomes have not been fully characterized. The single-arm, phase II NeoTENNIS trial evaluated neoadjuvant dose-dense epirubicin/cyclophosphamide followed by toripalimab plus nab-paclitaxel in patients with stage II-III TNBC. The protocol specified four neoadjuvant cycles of toripalimab, without mandatory continuation in the adjuvant setting. The primary endpoint was tpCR, and event-free survival (EFS) was a prespecified secondary endpoint. EFS was measured from the date of the first study dose. Among 70 enrolled patients, 62.9% had stage III disease. At a median follow-up of 44.7 months, 14 EFS events had occurred, and the estimated 3-year EFS rate was 80.6% (95% CI, 68.9-88.3%). The 3-year EFS rates were 92.2% and 66.0% in patients with and without tpCR, respectively. Non-tpCR was associated with inferior EFS in the multivariable model (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 4.20; 95% CI, 1.11-15.92). In exploratory genomic analyses, pathogenic germline BRCA1 variants (HR, 4.36; 95% CI, 1.15-16.59; P = 0.031) and somatic JAK2 amplification (HR, 6.61; 95% CI, 1.38-31.58; P = 0.018) were associated with inferior EFS. The platinum-free neoadjuvant NeoTENNIS regimen was associated with encouraging EFS in a predominantly stage III, node-positive population. These findings warrant further evaluation of this neoadjuvant de-escalation strategy in randomized clinical trials. papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal and treatment-refractory malignancies worldwide, largely driven by its uniquely desmoplastic and highly innervated microenvironment. Given the striking incidence of perineural invasion and its profound correlation with intractable cancer pain and early recurrence, tumor-nervous system crosstalk has emerged as a pivotal driver of PDAC progression. Neural components-including neurotransmitters, neurotrophic factors, axon guidance molecules, and specific sensory and autonomic networks (e.g., dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic nerves)-do not merely act as passive conduits, but actively orchestrate tumor genesis, metastasis, and immune evasion. Crucially, this neuro-stromal crosstalk actively drives chemoresistance by facilitating the dual-effect remodeling of tumor energy metabolism and detoxification networks. In this comprehensive review, we decode the multidimensional molecular mechanisms and reciprocal signaling cascades underpinning tumor-nervous system crosstalk. We critically evaluate the translational challenges of applying neurotherapy in clinical practice, encompassing mechanistic pleiotropy, neural plasticity, and visceral safety risks. Furthermore, by synthesizing emerging clinical trials targeting neurotransmitter axes, dorsal root ganglia, and neurotrophic signaling, we provide a forward-looking roadmap for integrating precision neuro-oncology with standard regimens to simultaneously alleviate cancer pain and overcome therapeutic resistance in PDAC.

papers.abstract: Brain metastases are a common and serious consequence for patients with renal cell carcinoma. This study aimed to determine if survival has changed since the introduction of current therapies, identify prognostic factors, update the prognostic index (the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment [GPA]) in the context of contemporary multi-modal therapies, compare outcomes with legacy cohorts, and determine whether overall survival correlates with intracranial progression-free survival. An international consortium of 21 academic institutions contributed uniformly-curated retrospective data from 1049 patients with newly-diagnosed renal cell carcinoma with brain metastases (RCC-BM) treated between Jan 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2022. Patients treated between 1985-2007 (n=286) and 2006-15 (n=711) were considered legacy cohorts and compared to the current cohort. Significant prognostic factors for survival were identified through combined multivariable analyses and used to update the Renal GPA. Intracranial progression-free survival was defined as the interval from date of initial RCC-BM diagnosis to date of first salvage treatment. Of the 1049 patients, 773 (73·7%) patients were male and 276 (26·3%) were female; the majority (851 [81·1%]) were White, and the median age was 63·9 years (IQR 56·2-70·3). The median overall survival was 20·0 months (95% CI 18·0-23·4), with a median follow-up of 53·4 months (95% CI 50·2-56·8). Overall survival for the legacy cohorts were 9·6 months (95% CI 8-11) and 12·0 months (5-11), respectively. In combined multivariable analyses, significant prognostic factors for inferior survival were lower Karnofsky Performance Status, lower baseline serum albumin, higher number of brain metastases, and presence of extracranial metastases. These factors were incorporated into the updated Renal GPA. Median survival was 4·8 months (95% CI 3·0-8·1) for patients with GPA 0-1·0, 12·4 months (10·6-17·2) for GPA 1·5-2·0, 33·6 months (27·5-40·0) for GPA 2·5-3·0, and 51·2 months (34·1-undefined) for GPA 3·5-4·0. Median intracranial progression-free survival was 9·6 months (95% CI 8·4-10·6). The Spearman's rank correlation between intracranial progression-free survival and overall survival was moderately strong (0·74 [95% CI 0·70-0·78]; p<0·0001). Survival has improved compared to the legacy cohorts but varies widely by GPA. The updated Renal GPA can be used to estimate survival, intracranial progression-free survival, individualise treatment, design and stratify clinical trials, and refine clinical trial eligibility. papers.abstract: Fractions of inspired oxygen up to 60% in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation are commonly perceived by clinicians as safe, implying a non-linear association between oxygen exposure and mortality. Also, although it seems pathophysiologically plausible that the association between oxygen exposure and mortality may depend on age, relevant evidence in adult patients is lacking. We examined whether the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality a) is non-linear and b) depends on age. We performed a secondary analysis of individual patient-level data from six acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) Network and PETAL Network randomized controlled trials ("ARDSNet cohort"). We assessed linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality along with the effect of age after adjusting for covariates, including partial pressure of arterial oxygen. We tested our findings in an independent multicenter cohort. In the ARDSNet cohort involving 4953 patients with ARDS, we found that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality was linear and independent of age (p = 0.655 for the interaction between fraction of inspired oxygen and age). In the independent cohort involving 559 patients with ARDS, we confirmed both the linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality and the lack of effect of age (p = 0.955 for the interaction). Data from the two tested multicenter cohorts suggest that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality in ARDS may be linear and independent of age.

papers.abstract: CPX-351, a liposomal formulation of cytarabine and daunorubicin, has been approved patients with secondary/high-risk acute myeloid leukemia including therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes according to the WHO 2016 classification. The aim of this study was to determine the efficacy and safety of CPX-351 in 283 patients with AML registered in the PETHEMA database. Evolving outcome results were analyzed comparing early treated patients (before-2022, N = 147) with those treated after Spanish financial approval (since-2022, N = 136). The CR/CRi rate was 54% in the overall cohort, without significant differences comparing both time periods. By contrast, early death rates at day + 30 and day + 60 were higher in early period patients (11.6 vs. 5.1% and 17 vs. 8.1%, p = 0.03 and p = 0.031). Consequently, more patients could undergo HSCT in the latter treatment period (33.8% vs. 25.2%, p = 0.04). Patients treated with CPX-351 since 2022 showed a significantly higher unadjusted 2-year OS probability compared with patients treated earlier [40.3% (95% CI: 26.3-62.4) versus 25.2% (95% CI: 18.6-34.1), P = 0.017]. However, treatment period was not independently associated with OS in multivariable analysis. Only TP53 wild-type status [HR 0.51 (95% CI: 0.25-1.05)] and achievement of MRD negativity after induction [HR 0.54 (95% CI: 0.29-1.0)] remained independently associated with improved OS. Overall, outcomes after CPX-351 appeared to improve over time in unadjusted analyses; however, the absence of an independent effect of treatment period and differences in patient selection between periods preclude attributing this improvement specifically to a temporal learning effect.

papers.abstract: Given the substantial chronic condition burden among adult survivors of childhood cancer, we explored associations between care coordination and discontinuity with patterns of care and health status. Data from Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (CCSS) participants with multiple chronic conditions who completed the validated CC-MC measure of care coordination and discontinuity in 2022 were linked with data from 2019 to 2021 on emergency department [ED] visits, hospitalizations, risk-based survivorship care advice, recommended screenings, and health status (SF-36, Brief Symptom Inventory [BSI-18]). Independent variables included three CC-MC coordination summary scores: main provider (knowing the patient and coordinating their care), multiple provider (coordinating care within and across clinics), patient-provider partnership (explaining things, considering patient goals); and discontinuity (dichotomous). Adjusted generalized linear models estimated prevalence ratios (PR), rate ratios (RR), and beta coefficients. Participants (n = 365) were mean age 48.2 years, 68.5% female, 90.1% non-Hispanic White. Better main provider (RR = 0.87; 95% CI: 0.77-0.99) and multiple provider (RR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.80-0.90) scores were associated with less ED use; better multiple provider scores with fewer hospitalizations (RR = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.81-0.96); and better patient-provider partnership scores with receiving risk-based survivorship care advice (PR = 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.08). We found no consistent associations between CC-MC scores and recommended screening, though screening rates were generally high. All three CC-MC summary scores were associated with fewer BSI global severity score elevations (PR range: 0.62-0.84). Discontinuity was associated with more hospitalizations (RR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.03-2.51) and BSI global severity score elevations (PR = 4.20; 95% CI: 1.74-10.16). Promoting care coordination across multiple providers and improving continuity may improve care and outcomes in this vulnerable population.

papers.abstract: Biliary Tract Cancers (BTCs) are difficult-to-treat malignancies with limited therapeutic options and dismal prognosis. Upfront comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is recommended for advanced BTC to identify actionable alterations, but its real-world implementation remains underexplored. In 2019, we implemented upfront CGP for advanced BTC at our institution. Molecular profiling results were reviewed within our institutional molecular tumor board when clinically applicable. Patients were followed throughout their disease course. A total of 80 patients with locally unresectable (n = 14) or metastatic (n = 66) BTC underwent CGP. Testing was performed on cytology material (6/80), tumor biopsies (38/80), or surgical specimens (36/80). In 59/80 cases (73.8%) testing was carried out prior to the beginning of palliative first-line treatment. In 42/80 (52.5%) cases, at least one clinically actionable genomic alteration was identified. The most frequent actionable alterations involved IDH1 (13.8%), FGFR2 (8.8%), ERBB2 (HER2) (5.0%), KRAS G12C (2.5%), and BRAF (1.3%). Alterations in DNA damage response genes were detected in 11/80 tumors, and 3/80 were dMMR/MSI-H. FGFR2 and IDH1 mutations were detected in ICC only, while HER2 alterations were more commonly detected in ECC and GBC. 11/42 patients with a clinically actionable alteration received targeted treatment during the disease course (1 first-line, 10 later lines). Among patients with an evaluable preceding systemic treatment line, treatment duration was longer with molecularly matched treatment than with the immediately preceding treatment line (p = 0.0391). 2/14 patients with initially unresectable BTC achieved secondary resectability during molecularly matched treatment. Upfront CGP is feasible in routine clinical practice and identifies clinically actionable alterations in a substantial proportion of patients with advanced BTC. However, only a subset received molecularly matched treatment, highlighting a gap between molecular actionability and treatment implementation. Timely access to matched therapies remains critical to the clinical utility of precision oncology in BTC.

papers.abstract: The MAGIC-D index was originally developed to predict outcomes in advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) patients receiving durvalumab-gemcitabine-cisplatin (Durva-Gem-Cis). This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of various durvalumab-chemotherapy regimens for unresectable BTC patients and the broader applicability of the MAGIC-D index. This study retrospectively recruited unresectable BTC patients receiving durvalumab-chemotherapy from 2021 to 2024. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed, and patients were risk-stratified using the MAGIC-D index. A total of 89 patients were included in the analysis. Between the Durva-Gem-Cis group and the durvalumab plus other chemotherapy regimens (Durva-Other Regimens) group, the median OS (12.9 vs. 13.9 months) and PFS (5.5 vs. 6.2 months) were comparable. Patients were risk-stratified into three risk groups (median OS: 21.0, 12.9, 12.4 months for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively; p = 0.002) using the MAGIC-D index, which achieved a concordance index (C-index) of 0.637. The Cox regression analysis showed serum CA 19-9 level, high Ki67 expression and the MAGIC-D index were related to OS. An exploratory model named the modified MAGIC-D index, incorporating Ki67 and CA 19-9 into the MAGIC-D index, showed promising discrimination of survival among risk groups (25.0 vs. 12.9 vs. 9.1 months, p < 0.001) with a C-index of 0.709. Durvalumab plus different chemotherapy regimens achieves comparable outcomes in the treatment of unresectable BTC. Incorporating Ki67 and CA 19-9 into the MAGIC-D index may enhance risk stratification, but external validation in larger independent cohorts is required before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Male breast cancer is rare, and data on its clinicopathological and germline characteristics remain scarce. Our objective was to describe the clinicopathological profile of men with breast cancer and to estimate the prevalence of pathogenic germline variants in cancer predisposition genes. This multicenter retrospective study included adult men diagnosed with breast cancer between January 2000 and June 2022 at two institutions. Clinical and pathological data were obtained from medical records. Germline analysis was performed in patients without prior testing using DNA from biobanks or saliva samples and a custom multigene panel. A total of 106 patients were included. Median age at diagnosis was 58.5 years (range, 33-84), and 64% reported a family history of cancer. Invasive ductal carcinoma was the predominant histological subtype (88%). Most tumors were grade 2 or 3 (90%) and hormone receptor-positive (93%). Hormone receptor-negative/HER2-positive disease was rare (1%), and triple-negative breast cancer accounted for 4% of cases. At diagnosis, 65% had stage II or III disease. Germline testing was performed in 55 patients, of whom 12 (22%) harbored pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. The most frequently affected gene was BRCA2 (11%), followed by CHEK2 (5.5%), MUTYH (3.6%), and RAD51C (1.8%). Male breast cancer in this cohort was predominantly luminal, high-grade, and frequently diagnosed at advanced stages. The high prevalence of germline pathogenic variants, including among patients without a strong family history, supports broader implementation of genetic counseling and multigene testing in this population.

papers.abstract: Although early-stage breast cancer incidence has increased following Korea's National Cancer Screening Program, the number of breast cancer-related deaths continues to rise, and many patients still present with symptoms. We investigated the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term prognosis of symptomatic versus asymptomatic breast cancer to determine whether symptomatic presentation serves as an independent prognostic factor. In this single-center, retrospective cohort study, we analyzed 38,050 women who underwent surgery for primary invasive breast cancer (1994-2021). Patients were categorized into symptomatic (N = 24,305) and asymptomatic (N = 13,745) groups. We used multivariable Cox models to adjust for confounders and conducted interaction analyses to assess prognostic factors and the impact of symptom presentation. Symptomatic patients were significantly younger than asymptomatic patients and presented with more advanced stages and aggressive biological features. Symptomatic presentation was associated with a significantly lower 10-year recurrence-free interval (P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, symptomatic status remained an independent predictor of worse outcomes (hazard ratio for recurrence, 1.44; 95% confidence interval, 1.33 to 1.57). Interaction analyses across subgroups defined by operation period, molecular subtype, and pathologic stage consistently showed that symptomatic presentation conferred a significantly higher risk of recurrence. Symptomatic breast cancer represents a clinically distinct presentation associated with adverse clinicopathologic features and persistently poorer long-term outcomes, even after adjustment for established prognostic factors. Despite the benefits of screening, the persistent burden of symptomatic disease underscores the need for public health strategies focused on early symptom awareness and regular breast self-examination.

papers.abstract: Hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer accounts for approximately 65-70% of all breast cancer cases. First-line treatment for metastatic HR+/HER2- disease typically includes endocrine therapy combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, achieving progression-free survival (PFS) of 24-33 months with preserved quality of life. Although CDK4/6 inhibitors are generally well tolerated, they are associated with hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicities. We describe a patient who developed features of chronic immune-mediate polyradiculoneuropathy associated with neurofascin antibodies following initiation of palbociclib. We conducted a detailed clinical review of a patient with metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer who developed progressive bilateral upper and lower extremity weakness after starting palbociclib. Clinical presentation, laboratory findings, imaging studies, electrodiagnostic testing, and treatment response were reviewed. A 43-year old female with metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer developed asymmetric progressive weakness and sensory symptoms approximately two weeks after initiating palbociclib. Electrodiagnostic testing demonstrated a mixed axonal and demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy meeting EAN/PNS criteria for an acquired inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Initial diagnostic considerations included acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP) and multifocal CIDP (formerly termed multifocal acquired demyelinating sensory and motor neuropathy [MADSAM]). Despite initial improvement following treatment with IVIG, the patient experienced continued neurologic progression requiring plasmapheresis, repeat IVIG, high-dose corticosteroids, and rituximab. Subsequent testing demonstrated anti-neurofascin-155 and anti-neurofascin-186 antibody positivity. Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated significant functional recovery following rituximab therapy. This case suggests a possible association between palbociclib exposure and the development of chronic immune-mediate polyradiculoneuropathy associated with neurofascin antibodies. Clinicians should consider immune mediated neuropathies in patients receiving CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy who develop weakness, sensory deficits, and areflexia. Further investigation is warranted to better characterize potential immunologic effects of CDK4/6 inhibition and their relationship to autoimmune neurologic disease.

papers.abstract: Prescription co-payments are associated with adherence to endocrine therapy among Medicare- and commercially insured-women, but the impact among Medicaid beneficiaries-who typically have no or minimal co-payments-is not well understood. We identified women (age ≥ 18 years) diagnosed with breast cancer between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2018 who filled a prescription for endocrine therapy after diagnosis, with follow-up through December 31, 2019. Co-payment was based on the first prescription and standardized to a 30-day supply. We used quantity dispensed, days' supply, and dispensing date to define adherence as a continuous measure of proportion of days covered and binary measure of +/- 80% days covered. We estimated associations with co-payment in linear and log binomial regression models limited to twenty states with observed within-state variation in co-payment. 10,307 Medicaid beneficiaries filled a prescription for endocrine therapy after breast cancer diagnosis. Mean (SD) co-payment amount was $1.85 ($1.28) and ranged from $0.17 to $8. Among 3,323 women living in states with variation in co-payment, there was no association between proportion of days covered and any co-payment (vs. none: β 0.70, p = 0.52) or co-payment amount (per dollar increase: β 0.03, p = 0.95), nor between adherence (≥ 80% days covered) and any co-payment (vs. none: PR 0.98, 95% CI 0.90, 1.08) or co-payment amount (per dollar increase: PR 0.99, 95% CI 0.96, 1.03). Most Medicaid-insured women with breast cancer had no or a nominal co-payment for endocrine therapy. Cost-sharing at these low levels was not associated with adherence.

papers.abstract: To investigate the association of molecular breast cancer subtypes with the timing and organ-specific patterns of metastatic disease. We analyzed data from nine German regional cancer registries, including 172 512 women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer between January 2000 and March 2024. Patients were classified as having no metastases, synchronous metastases (within three months of diagnosis), or metachronous metastases. Factors associated with synchronous metastases were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression adjusted for confounders. Time to first metachronous metastasis was analyzed using multivariable Cox regression. Timing and organ-specific metastatic patterns were compared across subtypes. Molecular subtypes were associated with both synchronous and metachronous metastatic disease. Compared with HR+/HER2- tumors, HR-/HER2+ tumors had the highest odds of synchronous metastasis (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.69, 95%CI 1.57 - 1.83), whereas HR-/HER2- tumors showed no increased odds (aOR 0.96, 95%CI 0.90 - 1.02). In contrast, HR-/HER2- tumors had the highest risk of metachronous metastases (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.48, 95%CI 1.41 - 1.55), while HR+/HER2+ tumors showed a lower risk than HR+/HER2- tumors (aHR 0.88, 95%CI 0.84-0.93). Cumulative incidence increased between 5 and 10 years after diagnosis, with late risk among HR-positive tumors. Metastatic patterns differed by subtype, with HR+/HER2- tumors showing predominantly bone metastases, and HR-/HER2- tumors exhibiting more frequent visceral and central nervous system (CNS) involvement. Molecular subtypes influence the timing and distribution of metastatic breast cancer. HER2-positive tumors are associated with synchronous metastatic presentation, whereas HR-/HER2- tumors showed the highest risk of metachronous metastasis. These findings support subtype-specific risk assessment and surveillance strategies.

papers.abstract: Repeat transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) is recommended for selected patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), but clinicopathologic indications are broad and often identify no residual tumor. We tested whether postresection urinary tumor DNA (utDNA) adds value beyond guideline-derived repeat-TURBT selection and established recurrence risk models. This guideline-anchored cohort analysis included 161 patients with NMIBC who underwent repeat TURBT. Urine was collected 2 to 6 weeks after initial TURBT and before repeat TURBT. Tissue-naïve utDNA and cytology were compared with repeat-TURBT pathology and evaluated against repeat-TURBT indication sets, European Association of Urology (EAU) risk grouping, The European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) models, and Club Urologico Espanol de Tratamiento Oncologico (CUETO) models. Residual tumor was found in 57 patients (35.4%). Core, expanded, and carcinoma in situ-augmented core indication sets selected 73.3%, 88.2%, and 80.7% of patients. Within these indication-positive groups, utDNA-negative status identified 66.9% to 67.7% as lower-yield, although 9.1% to 10.4% still had residual tumor. Adding utDNA increased residual tumor AUCs from 0.544 to 0.891, 0.537 to 0.892, and 0.513 to 0.890 for the three indication sets, respectively. For any recurrence, c-indices increased from 0.602 to 0.774 for EAU risk grouping, 0.717 to 0.837 for EORTC models, and 0.770 to 0.824 for CUETO models after adding utDNA. Postresection utDNA refined residual tumor detection beyond repeat-TURBT indication sets and improved recurrence risk stratification beyond EAU/EORTC models, with directionally consistent CUETO results. Positive utDNA after negative repeat TURBT suggested occult molecular risk and supports prospective testing of utDNA-informed resection and surveillance algorithms.

papers.abstract: T cell receptors (TCRs) can enable detection and elimination of cancer cells via recognition of cancer-specific peptides presented on human leukocyte antigen (HLA). We speculated that shared cancer antigens could be recognized by recurrent ("public") TCRs, which might be identifiable using statistical methods. Here, we identified public TCRs against therapeutically relevant targets via computational analysis of large-scale bulk RNA sequencing data obtained from routine clinical genomics testing. Using data from ∼150,000 patient tumor samples, we identified TCR chains that were associated with well-known cancer antigens, including human papillomavirus, mutated KRAS, and CT83. We devised methods for pairing enriched TCR-α and TCR-β chain sequences and validated 44 TCRs across nine peptide-HLA targets for antigen recognition, including potent cytotoxic TCRs. Our results suggest that public anticancer TCRs are common and may represent a new source for the development of cancer therapeutics.

papers.abstract: Enzalutamide (Enz)-resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as an N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m6A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m6A-dependent translational regulation.

papers.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m6A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

papers.abstract: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer. Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample. At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group. Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels. papers.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) is an established treatment for peritoneal surface malignancies, but is associated with substantial morbidity, particularly when pelvic anastomoses are performed. Diverting ostomies are commonly used to mitigate complications related to anastomotic leak; however, ostomy formation carries its own morbidity, and its benefit in this setting remains controversial. PubMed and Embase were queried for studies of patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis, documented use of diverting ostomy, and reported anastomotic leak rates. Eligible studies required combined CRS/HIPEC, explicit reporting of diversion status, and perioperative outcomes stratified by ostomy presence. Abstracts were independently screened by two reviewers, followed by full-text review for final inclusion. A binary odds ratio meta-analysis was performed comparing anastomotic leak between diverted and non-diverted patients. Of 506 studies identified, 10 met inclusion criteria and were combined with our institutional cohort, comprising 1506 patients. Overall, diversion was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.32-1.39, p = 0.28). No differences were observed in grade ≥ 3 complications or length of stay. Diversion was associated with increased 60-day readmissions (OR 3.29, 95% CI 1.52-7.11, p < 0.01). Diverting ostomies were not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak in patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis. These findings suggest consideration of a selective, rather than routine, diversion strategy in appropriately selected patients.

papers.abstract: Adoptive cell therapies using chimeric antigen receptor or T cell receptor-transgenic T cells (TCR-T) are effective in treating hematological malignancies but have limited efficacy in solid tumors, particularly brain tumors. A major challenge of adoptive T cell therapy in brain tumors is lack of access to the target antigen, which is necessary for restimulation and persistence. Here, we addressed this challenge by using an mRNA vaccine encoding the cognate antigen to induce in vivo restimulation of transferred TCR-T cells in glioma models. Delivery of mRNA encoding the immunodominant MHC class I ovalbumin epitope SIINFEKL to splenic dendritic cells initiated strong expansion of adoptively transferred ovalbumin-specific OT1 CD8+ T cells to up to 80% of all circulating CD8+ T cells. RNA vaccination markedly improved T cell infiltration and retained interferon-stimulated gene signature in the brain, suppressing glioblastoma growth. The therapeutic efficacy of this approach was further demonstrated in an experimental model for a first-in-class TCR-T cell therapy targeting an HLA-A2-restricted immunodominant epitope of the human glioblastoma stemness antigen PTPRZ1. Co-administration of human dendritic cells transfected with PTPRZ1-mRNA led to rejection of orthotopically implanted primary human gliomas endogenously expressing PTPRZ1 and HLA-A2 after adoptive transfer of PTPRZ1-TCR-T cells. In summary, these findings indicate that mRNA vaccines can boost TCR-T cell therapy against glioblastoma.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)-high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-Ihigh contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8+ T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8+ T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor- and chimeric antigen receptor-based immunotherapies in IFN-Ihigh tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-Ihigh / IFNAR1low axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.abstract: Several tRNAs that differ only in their body sequence decode the same codon, yet their levels and behavior vary across cell types and disease contexts. In a landmark 2014 study, a mutation in the arginine isodecoder Arg-TCT-4 was linked to neurodegeneration in mice. In 2021, increased expression of the Arg-TCT family, especially Arg-TCT-4, was unexpectedly linked to oncogenic transformation in multiple cancer models. A recent publication by Kim and colleagues reports that loss of a single tRNA isodecoder, Arg-TCT-1, drives lineage plasticity and resistance to androgen receptor pathway inhibitors in prostate cancer by reducing the translation of AGA-rich mRNAs. Together, these findings raise a broader question: what do differences in isodecoder sequence actually do? They may influence tRNA processing, charging, interactions with elongation factors and the ribosome, or the modifications tRNAs receive. This commentary places the new findings in the context of prior work and considers potential mechanisms behind the functional diversity of Arg-TCT isodecoders and their role in cancer.

papers.abstract: Targeted biologics have transformed the treatment of inflammatory skin diseases such as plaque psoriasis. However, some patients with psoriasis paradoxically develop eczematous skin reactions after therapy targeting tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), or IL-23. Although paradoxical eczema (PE) resembles atopic dermatitis (AD) clinically and histologically, the molecular mechanisms that drive its development remain poorly understood. Here, we generated high-resolution cellular and spatial maps of human skin using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, and in vitro assays, profiling lesional biopsies from patients with PE (n = 8 donors), alongside healthy control, psoriasis, and AD skin (n = 4 donors per group). In PE, we identified distinct transcriptional changes characterized by myeloid and T cell expansion and an altered keratinocyte phenotype shaped by TNF-like weak inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK; encoded by TNFSF12) signaling through its receptor TNFRSF12A, confirmed at the protein level by immunohistochemistry. To define the underlying mechanism, we stimulated immortalized (N-TERT) and primary human keratinocytes and found that TWEAK acted together with IL-13 to drive a T helper 2- and type I interferon-polarized epithelial program that partially recapitulated the keratinocyte signature of PE lesions. We validated key target genes by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in primary keratinocytes. In THP-1 cells and primary human CD14+ monocytes, anti-TNF treatment induced TWEAK expression, suggesting a compensatory inflammatory circuit. Together, these findings identify the TWEAK-IL-13 axis as a key driver of PE and suggest how cytokine blockade may reshape cutaneous immune responses.

papers.abstract: Previous studies combining the multikinase inhibitor regorafenib with a PD-1 inhibitor showed promising activity in gastric cancer. We conducted a phase 1b/2 trial (NCT05394740) of first-line regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy in 30 patients with mismatch repair-proficient gastric cancer and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment. The primary end point was met; 22 of 30 patients showed objective tumor response (73%; 80% confidence interval, 60.3 to 83.8). Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing were performed on biopsy samples at baseline, during treatment, and at disease progression. The combination treatment increased tumor antigen-reactive CD8+ T cells and M1-like proinflammatory macrophages and decreased immunosuppressive and tumor-promoting populations, including activated CCR8+ regulatory T cells, LRRC15+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), RGS5+ pericytes, and APLN+ tip cells. At progression, LRRC15+ CAFs and APLN+ tip cells remained reduced, activated CCR8+ regulatory T cells reexpanded, and additional treatment-resistant subsets emerged, including APOC1+ lipid-associated macrophages. In murine models of acquired resistance, therapeutic targeting of these suppressive immune cell populations with antibodies against CCR8 or TREM2 in combination with PD-1 blockade restored antitumor immunity. These findings demonstrate dynamic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract: Oxaliplatin-related neuropathy (OIPN) remains a frequent chemotherapy-induced complication, yet its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence implicates pyroptosis in OIPN pathogenesis, and palmitoylation has been recognised as a critical mechanism in neurological disorders. This investigation set out to examine the part played by the palmitoyltransferase Zdhhc14 in pyroptosis in OIPN as well as to clarify the fundamental molecular processes. A mouse model of OIPN was developed through intraperitoneal oxaliplatin administration, and primary neuronal cultures derived from dorsal root ganglia were exposed to oxaliplatin to simulate OIPN in vitro. Bioinformatics analysis was performed using the GSE255097 dataset. Gene and protein expression were examined by quantitative real-time PCR, Western blot and immunofluorescence staining. Pyroptosis was assessed by lactate dehydrogenase release, flow cytometry and detection of pyroptosis-related proteins. Co-immunoprecipitation, immunoprecipitation and cycloheximide chase assay were applied to evaluate the mechanisms. Zdhhc14 was significantly up-regulated in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) of OIPN mice in a time-dependent manner. Zdhhc14 deficiency alleviated OIPN phenotypes, including mechanical hyperalgesia and cold allodynia, neuroinflammation and DRG pyroptosis. Mechanistically, Zdhhc14 binds to GBP5 and promotes its modification at Cys12, which is required for Zdhhc14-mediated suppression of K48-linked ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation, thereby stabilising GBP5. GBP5 knockdown phenocopied the protective effects of Zdhhc14 deficiency, whereas GBP5 overexpression reversed these effects. Importantly, mutation of the GBP5 palmitoylation site abolished the pro-pyroptotic effects of Zdhhc14. These findings indicate that the Zdhhc14/GBP5 palmitoylation axis critically regulates DRG pyroptosis and neuroinflammation in OIPN, identifying a novel mechanism and a potential mechanistic target warranting further translational evaluation for this debilitating condition.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) has a high incidence in East Asia, yet early detection remains limited. In this multiphase study, 395 participants (96 GC, 72 precancerous lesions, 227 healthy donors) were enrolled. Plasma IFNL3 levels were measured using ELISA. Mendelian randomization was used to assess the causality between IFNL3 and GC. Receiver operating characteristic curves were used to calculate diagnostic efficiency in comparison between IFNL3 and traditional biomarkers (alpha fetoprotein [AFP], carcinoembryonic antigen [CEA], and cancer antigen 19-9 [CA19-9]). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analysis suggested a potential association between plasma IFNL3 and GC in East Asians. In Test phase, plasma IFNL3 demonstrated superior diagnostic performance in differentiating GC from HDs (AUC = 0.901, 95% CI: 0.866-0.935) compared to AFP, CEA, and CA19-9. IFNL3 levels correlated with disease progression, increasing progressively across clinical stages. IFNL3 mRNA was also higher in cancerous tissues compared to normal and para-cancerous tissues. In Validation phase, IFNL3 exhibited high diagnostic specificity. In Extension phase, plasma IFNL3 showed distinct diagnostic potential for differentiating chronic non-atrophic gastritis (CNAG), atrophic intestinal metaplasia (AIM), low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (LGIN), and high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN). Plasma IFNL3 levels were increased in gastric cancer and correlated with disease progression. However, its value as a diagnostic biomarker requires validation in larger, stage-adjusted studies.

papers.abstract: Overcoming resistance to standard-of-care chemotherapy represents an unmet need in oncology. To help address this challenge, here we established and characterized a panel of human cisplatin-resistant lung and breast cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids from high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas (HGSOC), and show that platinum resistance can be overcome by treatment with diethyldithiocarbamate-copper (CuET), a metabolite of the alcohol-aversion drug disulfiram. All platinum-resistant models remained sensitive to CuET, consistent with distinct cytotoxicity mechanisms: proteotoxic stress for CuET and DNA damage for cisplatin, respectively. Platinum adduct and DNA damage response analyses suggested diverse mechanisms of cisplatin resistance among our models. Considering potential CuET-based therapies, our gene knock-down and functional assays in preclinical models, complemented with immunohistochemical analysis of tissue samples from cohorts of triple-negative breast cancer and HGSOC patients indicate that levels of metallothioneins, rather than NPL4 (the molecular target of CuET) warrant further evaluation as candidate biomarkers of CuET sensitivity. This dataset provides a resource of platinum-resistant models of common carcinomas, identifies CuET as a compound overcoming such resistance and provides leads for predictive biomarker discovery, with potential clinical implications in oncology.

papers.abstract: Rates of cancer cure increase; however, recurrence and refractoriness remain clinical challenges that require alternative therapeutic strategies. Natural killer (NK) cells could play a decisive role if their antitumor reactivity can be enhanced. The interaction between killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIRs) and their human leukocyte antigen class-I (HLA-I) ligands significantly influences NK-cell education and may impact clinical outcomes in cancer patients. In this study, we evaluated the impact of KIR/HLA-I interactions on the transcriptomic profile of circulating NK-cells and their association with patient outcome. KIR and HLA-I genotyping, together with KIR expression analysis in circulating NK cells, were performed in patients with solid and hematologic malignancies (n = 1,153). In addition, single-cell transcriptomic analyses (scRNA-seq) of circulating NK and T lymphocytes were carried out in selected donors with KIR/HLA-I genotypes associated with short and long survival. Activating KIRs (aKIRs), more than inhibitory KIRs, were associated with cancer patient outcomes. The accumulation of aKIR-HLA interactions was related to shorter overall survival, whereas KIR2DS1/C2 interaction, in the absence of other aKIR interactions, was associated with longer survival. Three major NK-cell transcriptional profiles were identified: mature cytotoxic, immature/regulatory, and adaptive cytotoxic. The adaptive-like transcriptional profile was associated with longer survival. In conclusion, aKIR/HLA-I interactions were associated with cancer patient outcomes. In particular, KIR2DS1/C2 interaction in the absence of other activating signals was associated with adaptive NK-cell transcriptomic profiles and improved survival. Understanding the mechanisms underlying effective NK-cell-mediated tumor immunity may provide new opportunities for patients with refractory tumors.

papers.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most prevalent and disabling neurological disorders, affecting >50 million people worldwide. Beyond recurrent seizures, it is strongly associated with cognitive impairment, psychiatric comorbidities, reduced social participation, and a markedly increased risk of premature death. Although considerable advances in neuroimaging, pharmacology, and surgical techniques have expanded therapeutic possibilities, nearly one-third of patients remain refractory to current treatments, a challenge that highlights the pressing need for deeper mechanistic insights and innovative therapeutic strategies. This review provides an integrated overview of recent progress in epilepsy research and treatment. At the molecular level, we examine how ion channel dysfunction, receptor abnormalities, and disrupted signaling pathways drive hyperexcitability. We highlight insights from genetics and acquired etiologies that illuminate disease heterogeneity. We address prevailing hypotheses of drug resistance and potential biomarkers. We also emphasize the growing recognition of epilepsy's close association with diverse comorbidities, where shared molecular pathways not only deepen our understanding of disease mechanisms but also highlight new therapeutic targets. Finally, we evaluate emerging therapeutic directions, including precision pharmacology, neuromodulation, gene and cell therapies, and metabolic approaches such as the ketogenic diet. By bridging epidemiological perspectives with mechanistic discoveries and innovative therapies, this review underscores how advances in epilepsy research are reshaping the path toward precision medicine and improved patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Oculo-Cerebro-Renal-Lowe syndrome, caused by loss of the PI(4,5)P₂ 5-phosphatase OCRL, is a rare and severe disorder that lacks curative therapy. By integrating deep cell-biological insight into endosomal trafficking and proximal tubule protein reabsorption with high-content screening across engineered cell lines, patient-derived proximal tubule cells, human kidney organoids, and a humanized mouse model, we identify IB-MECA, an oral adenosine A3 receptor agonist, as a targeted therapy poised for clinical evaluation. IB-MECA normalizes endosomal PI(4,5)P₂ homeostasis, restores receptor trafficking, and rescues protein reabsorption in all systems, demonstrating the translational power of a mechanism-anchored, cross-species screening pipeline that couples cellular correction to organ-level benefit and supports rapid progression toward phase II testing pending regulatory approval. Mechanistic dissection revealed that IB-MECA acts through A3AR-dependent activation of PLC, revealing a previously unrecognized axis whereby receptor-driven hydrolysis of plasma-membrane PI(4,5)P₂ corrects pathological endosomal PI(4,5)P₂ accumulation. This receptor-mediated rewiring of phosphoinositide homeostasis contrasts with earlier strategies based on broad kinase inhibition and establishes plasma-membrane GPCR-PLC signaling as a precise, druggable entry point to correct endolysosomal lipid imbalance. Together with the favorable clinical safety record of IB-MECA, these findings provide a compelling rationale for an imminent clinical trial (NCT07410455) in Lowe syndrome and outline a generalizable, cell biology-guided framework for developing therapies for inherited disorders of phosphoinositide metabolism.

papers.abstract: Choroid plexus tumours (CPTs) are rare intraventricular brain neoplasms derived from choroid plexus epithelium, predominantly affecting young children. They include benign choroid plexus papilloma (CPP), atypical CPP (aCPP), and malignant choroid plexus carcinoma (CPC) and segregate into three DNA-methylation subgroups: paediatric A (pedA), paediatric B (pedB), and adult. To resolve subtype-specific biology, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing on 43 CPTs and integrated 12 non-neoplastic foetal, paediatric, and adult choroid plexus references, complemented by spatial transcriptomics in a subset of 16 tumour sections and 2 normal choroid plexus samples. Tumour embeddings and correlation analyses demonstrated that CPTs cluster by methylation subtype rather than WHO grade, revealing epigenetically driven relationships despite divergent histology. We identified 10 tumour metaprograms spanning epithelial differentiation, ciliogenesis, proliferation, extra cellular matrix remodelling, and stress responses. PedA and adult tumours showed relatively homogeneous program distribution dominated by differentiation or ciliation states, whereas pedB tumours exhibited marked heterogeneity with selective enrichment of hypoxia, interferon signalling, early stress response, and TGF-β signalling. Spatial mapping revealed consistent anticorrelation of these programs with ciliogenesis and differentiation programs, suggesting stress-associated dedifferentiation. Elevated stress and hypoxia scores correlated with poorer survival. PedB tumours showed enrichment of interferon- and lipid-associated myeloid populations, that carried pro-angiogenic signatures. They were spatially co-localised with hypoxic and interferon I expressing tumour areas, that were predicted to interact with myeloid cells via immunosuppressive cues, shaping a pro-angiogenic, pro-tumour environment. This study identifies stress- and hypoxia-associated dedifferentiation programs that are selectively enriched in pedB tumours, correlate with poor clinical outcome, and antagonise multiciliogenesis and epithelial differentiation. Their spatial co-localisation with immunosuppressive, pro-angiogenic macrophage populations links developmental arrest to microenvironmental remodelling and aggressive behaviour. These findings provide a biologically grounded framework for risk stratification and highlight hypoxia, angiogenesis and macrophage polarisation as candidate therapeutic targets in high-risk CPTs.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance. We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier. We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4+ TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort. Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

papers.abstract: Surgical resection for recurrent pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains controversial, and selection criteria are lacking. This study evaluated long-term outcomes after curative-intent resection for recurrent PDAC and examined whether preoperative biologic factors stratify prognosis. Patients undergoing curative-intent resection for recurrent PDAC after pancreatectomy between 2005 and 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Overall survival (OS) and predictors of early recurrence (≤6 months) were assessed using uni- and multivariable analyses. Resection for recurrent PDAC was performed for 44 patients. The median survival time (MST) was 32.9 months. Survival differed by recurrence site. The MSTs for the lung, liver, remnant pancreas, and other sites were 62.4, 18.9, 19.3, and 16.5 months, respectively (p = 0.075). Multivariable analysis showed that a CA19-9 concentration higher than 100 U/mL (hazard ratio [HR], 3.20; p = 0.004) and a prognostic nutritional index (PNI) lower than 45 (HR, 3.89; p < 0.001) independently predicted poor OS. Composite CA19-9 and PNI stratification showed three prognostic groups, low-risk (both favorable), intermediate-risk (either favorable), and high-risk (both unfavorable), with MSTs of 61.7, 12.4, and 8.1 months, respectively (p < 0.001). Among the patients with pulmonary recurrence, the low-risk group achieved an MST of 91.5 months, whereas among those with hepatic recurrence, the low-risk group achieved an MST of 55.5 months. A low PNI independently predicted early recurrence (p = 0.040). Increased tumor marker burden and impaired immunonutritional status were associated with poor survival after resection for recurrent PDAC. Integrating tumor biology and host condition into preoperative assessments may inform multidisciplinary surgical decision-making and help prevent futile resection.
