papers.abstract: Women undergoing mastectomy for early-stage breast cancer experience physical, emotional, and psychosocial sequalae after surgery. This impact on women's identity, body image, and self-esteem is often studied in isolation, limiting the ability to capture the multidimensional nature of post-mastectomy recovery. Our systematic review aimed to characterize the range of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) used to assess postoperative psychosocial experiences. Three databases were queried for relevant articles from January 1, 1997 to October 25, 2024 using keywords and controlled vocabulary for mastectomy, patient reported outcome measures, and psychology. Twenty studies met inclusion criteria. Most were single-institution, cross-sectional studies. More than half of the studies (60%) reported a mean or median participant age between 50-60 years. Most studies that reported participant race (72%) included > 80% White women. Thirty-eight different PROMs were used across 15 studies. Most instruments were used in only one study. Three studies developed their own measures. Seven psychosocial domains were identified: quality of life, sexual health/sexual function, body image, mental health, pain/physical health, psychosocial health, and satisfaction. Compared with mastectomy, breast conservation surgery was associated with better body image (67%) and physical health (38%) as well as improved psychosocial outcomes and satisfaction; reconstruction improved but did not eliminate these differences. Mastectomy is associated with poor psychosocial outcomes across multiple domains, yet this is often disregarded as a critical component of postoperative recovery. These findings highlight the critical need to better prepare women for mastectomy and identify tailored support strategies to improve patient-reported outcomes. The study protocol was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (Registration number: CRD42024XXXXXX).

papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are chronic diseases characterized by an excessive production of myeloid blood cells. Janus kinase (JAK2)V617F is the most common mutation in MPNs but a substantial proportion of patients harbour calreticulin (CALR) mutations-an attractive target for emerging immunotherapies. Natural killer (NK) cells have a central role in the elimination of malignant cells, but NK cells of MPN patients have reduced activity. Thus, reactivating their function might improve the disease outcome. Here, we demonstrate that NK cells from a CALR-mutant mouse model exhibit normal maturation but enhanced degranulation. Consistently, NK cells from CALR-mutant patients exhibit preserved degranulation ability, exceeding that observed in JAK2-mutant patients. Notably, NK cells from CALR-, but not JAK2-mutant patients express high levels of the immune checkpoint TIGIT possibly due to increased abundance of immunomodulatory proteins in the plasma. Moreover, CD34⁺ cells from MPN patients express elevated levels of the TIGIT ligand CD112. TIGIT blockade results in reduced platelet numbers in a transplant mouse model. These findings suggest that NK cells in CALR-mutant MPNs are activated but functionally constrained when encountering TIGIT ligand-expressing target cells, providing a strong rationale for exploring TIGIT blockade to restore NK-cell immunity in this disease subset.

papers.abstract: The clinical significance of homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations beyond BRCA2 in advanced prostate cancer is poorly understood. We investigated the association of individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations with outcomes of patients treated with first-line therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Eligible patients from the prospective CAPTURE study underwent somatic/germ line DNA analyses using a next-generation sequencing panel including ATM, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, HDAC2, PALB2, RAD51B, and RAD54L. Association with overall survival (OS) and radiographic progression-free survival was assessed using multivariable Cox regression models comparing individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations to those in patients with BRCA2 alterations or without HRR alterations. A total of 1010 patients were included, with BRCA2 and non-BRCA2 HRR alterations found in 122 (12%) and 191 (19%) patients, respectively. BRCA1, ATM, FANCA, HDAC2, CHEK2, CDK12, and BRIP1 alterations were observed in 19 (1.9%), 69 (6.8%), 34 (3.4%), 24 (2.4%), 23 (2.3%), 20 (2%), and 15 (1.5%) patients, respectively. Patients with ATM (hazard ratio [HR] 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.30; p = 0.002) or CHEK2 (HR 1.71; 95% CI = 1.03-2.90; p = 0.039) alterations showed improved OS compared to patients with BRCA2 alterations, with similar outcomes to patients without HRR alterations. BRCA1 (HR 0.49; 95% CI = 0.30-0.80; p = 0.004), FANCA (HR 0.61; 95% CI = 0.42-0.89; p = 0.011), and CDK12 (HR 0.57; 95% CI = 0.35-0.93; p = 0.025) were associated with worse OS compared to patients without HRR alterations, with similar outcomes to patients with BRCA2 alterations. Prognostic associations differ across individual HRR alterations. Although BRCA1, FANCA, or HDAC mutations were associated with a prognosis similar to that associated with BRCA2 alterations, prognosis in patients with ATM or CHEK2 alterations was similar to that in patients without HRR alterations. In the research setting, non-BRCA2 HRR alterations should be analyzed and reported as individual entities whenever possible.

papers.abstract: Contemporary risk stratification of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant lower-grade gliomas relies primarily on molecular characteristics and surgical tumor burden but does not capture dynamic tumor behavior. Our primary objective was to determine whether pretherapeutic tumor growth velocity (TGV) provides independent prognostic information for overall survival (OS) beyond established factors. This multicenter retrospective study included 569 adults with grade 2-3 IDH-mutant gliomas from three French centers, comprising a development cohort (n = 440) and two external validation cohorts (n = 129). TGV was derived from automated, outcome-blinded volumetric analysis of serial preoperative MRI using mean diameter expansion and log-volume growth. Prognostic value was assessed using multivariable Cox regression, external validation, decision curve analysis, and exploratory random survival forests. During a median follow-up of 6.8 years, 73 deaths occurred in the development cohort. Higher TGV was independently associated with shorter overall survival after adjustment for age, sex, grade, 1p/19q status, and postoperative residual tumor volume (HR per 1-mm/year increase, 1.046; 95%CI, 1.011-1.083; P=.011), and was independently replicated externally (HR, 1.077; 95% CI, 1.005-1.153; P=.035). Findings were consistent using log-volume growth and after accounting for CDKN2A/B status. Adding TGV improved prognostic model fit (likelihood-ratio χ²=5.70; P=.017), with greatest incremental value in astrocytomas. Decision curve analysis demonstrated additional clinical utility, while survival forests identified TGV among the strongest survival predictors alongside 1p/19q status and postoperative residual tumor volume. Pretherapeutic TGV independently predicts survival beyond contemporary molecular and surgical factors in IDH-mutant lower-grade gliomas. This accessible MRI-derived biomarker may refine individualized risk stratification, particularly in astrocytoma.

papers.abstract: To determine whether identical HPV-human DNA integrations in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) lesions are retained during progression to squamous cervical carcinoma (SCC) and whether such integrations can predict lesion persistence or progression. Longitudinal cervical samples were analyzed using multiplexed DNA hybridization-capture targeting 225 HPV types, followed by short-read sequencing to identify HPV-human DNA integration junctions. Integration events were evaluated in (i) serial samples from CIN lesions that progressed to SCC and (ii) a baseline cohort of 23 patients with incident CIN2. Clinical outcomes (regression vs persistence/progression) were compared by integration status using Fisher's Exact Test and multivariable Bayesian logistic regression to estimate effect sizes in the setting of small sample size. Identical HPV-human DNA integrations were preserved across serial samples in seven CIN lesions that progressed to SCC, supporting their biological relevance in carcinogenesis. In the CIN2 cohort, no integrations were detected in any of the 12 patients whose lesions regressed, whereas integrations were present in four of eleven patients whose lesions persisted or progressed (p=0.04). Bayesian logistic regression estimated a 22-fold higher odds of persistence/progression when integration was detected at baseline CIN2 diagnosis. HPV16 positivity was also associated with persistence/progression, with a smaller estimated effect size (9.4-fold higher odds), consistent with prior epidemiologic observations. HPV DNA integrations were associated with CIN2 persistence and progression, and identical integrations were retained during evolution to SCC. Integration analysis at CIN2 diagnosis may identify lesions at highest risk for progression, providing a biomarker to refine clinical management and reduce unnecessary excisional procedures.

papers.abstract: To develop an interpretable dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLCT) model for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and to compare two-dimensional region-of-interest (2D ROI) with whole-tumor three-dimensional volume-of-interest (3D VOI) parameter-extraction strategies. This retrospective study included 205 surgically treated patients with CSCC who underwent contrast-enhanced DLCT before surgery. Patients were assigned to training (n = 113), internal validation (n = 47), and temporal validation (n = 45) cohorts. Parameters were extracted using 2D ROI- and 3D VOI-based analyses. Clinical, 2D DLCT, 3D DLCT, and DLCT-clinical fusion models were developed using multivariable logistic regression and evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. 3D VOI-based analysis showed higher interobserver reproducibility than 2D ROI-based analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.950 vs. 0.875; P < 0.001). The 3D DLCT model included arterial-phase 70-keV virtual monoenergetic attenuation (CT70keV-AP), arterial-phase normalized effective atomic number (NZeffAP), and venous-phase normalized iodine density (NIDVP). Its areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.897, 0.895, and 0.885 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation cohorts, respectively. The 2D DLCT and 3D DLCT models did not differ significantly in AUCs after multiple-comparison correction. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.900, 0.916, and 0.881, respectively, outperforming the clinical model without significantly improving on the 3D DLCT model. 3D DLCT quantification provides an interpretable and noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated CSCC and may support individualized risk stratification. External validation in larger multicenter cohorts is needed to confirm generalizability.

papers.abstract: Imaging surveillance for pancreatic cancer (PC) is recommended for select high-risk individuals (HRIs) with a goal of downstaging PC diagnosis and improving long-term survival. A common subgroup of HRIs undergoing PC surveillance imaging includes those with a heterozygous pathogenic germline variant (PGV) in breast cancer susceptibility genes BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, or PALB2. Despite expanding recommendations for PC surveillance imaging in these individuals, limited evidence exists to guide counseling regarding the frequency and longitudinal outcomes of imaging findings. The Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection (PRECEDE) Consortium is a prospective multicenter cohort study of HRIs undergoing PC surveillance imaging. In this study, we report imaging outcomes across the first 5 years of enrollment (April 2020-April 2025) for PRECEDE participants with a heterozygous PGV in BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, or PALB2. Among 2,085 eligible participants, PGVs in BRCA2 (51%) were most common, followed by BRCA1 (21%), ATM (19%), and PALB2 (9%). Baseline pancreatic imaging occurred primarily with endoscopic ultrasound (EUS; 55%) or magnetic resonance imaging (43%). More than half (54%) of the participants had at least 1 pancreatic imaging finding during the study, while concerning findings including worrisome cysts, main pancreatic duct dilation ≥5 mm, and solid masses were detected in 9.1% of the cohort. Among HRIs without a pancreatic cyst or solid mass at baseline imaging, 71% remained without findings after at least two follow-ups. Additionally, 87% of HRIs with pancreatic cysts and follow-up imaging using the same modality did not have worrisome cyst growth. In this largest reported cohort of BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, and PALB2 heterozygotes undergoing PC surveillance imaging, benign/low-risk pancreatic imaging findings were common and stable on short-term follow-up, providing important data for counseling these HRIs.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is a spatially heterogeneous disease in which signaling transitions driving progression remain poorly defined, because bulk molecular analyses obscure compartment-specific pathway alterations. To resolve spatial signaling organization within human tumors, we performed intra-patient, lesion-matched profiling of MRI-targeted biopsies from the same prostate, focusing on Protein Kinase A (PKA). Immunofluorescence across healthy, Grade Group 1, and Grade Group 4 tissues revealed progressive redistribution of PKA subunits: RIβ expression declined with basal layer disruption, whereas PKAC was redistributed to proliferating tumor cells, establishing a grade-dependent imbalance between regulatory and catalytic components. This redistribution was associated with increased phosphorylation of PKA substrates, linking subunit distribution to pathway activation. Quantitative image analysis and biochemical validation of matched suspicious and non-suspicious biopsy cores from 40 patients confirmed coordinated changes in subunit expression and elevated pathway activity. Analysis of independent proteomics datasets comprising over 400 cases further supported dysregulation of catalytic-to-regulatory PKA balance and revealed enrichment of PKA phosphorylation motifs among recurrence-associated proteins. Together, these findings define a spatial transition in PKA regulatory control and support a model in which spatial redistribution of signaling components contributes to pathway activation in heterogeneous tumors.

papers.abstract: Oxaliplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) is increasingly used in locally advanced colorectal cancer (CRC); however, early acquired resistance substantially limits its efficacy. We revealed an enrichment of therapy-induced senescence (TIS)-like phenotypes in short-term oxaliplatin-exposed CRC. Consistently, a similar upregulation of senescence markers was observed in oxaliplatin-resistant CRC cells. Senolytic treatment attenuated senescence features and restored oxaliplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo. Integrative analysis of RNA-sequencing data from resistant tumours and ABT263-treated resistant tumours identified adenosine A1 receptor (ADORA1) as a key mediator of senescence and oxaliplatin resistance. ADORA1 is highly expressed in CRC tumours and is further induced by oxaliplatin, with elevated ADORA1 levels enriched in chemoresistant patients and associated with poor outcomes following chemotherapy. Mechanistically, ADORA1 directly interacts with and stabilises fatty acid synthase (FASN) by suppressing its ubiquitin-mediated degradation, thereby promoting palmitic acid (PA) synthesis, lipid droplet accumulation and p53/p21-driven senescence. Conversely, ADORA1 knockdown attenuates these phenotypes and restores oxaliplatin sensitivity. Together, these findings identify the ADORA1-FASN-PA metabolic reprogramming as a central mechanistic link between TIS and oxaliplatin resistance in CRC, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming early acquired resistance.

papers.abstract: Mobile element insertions (MEIs) shape the human genome in both germline and somatic tissues. While inherited MEIs are well characterized, identifying somatic MEIs (sMEIs) in non-cancer tissues remains challenging due to their low allelic fraction and repetitive nature. Here, we present an integrative framework for sMEI mapping that leverages modern sequencing technologies and analytical innovations. We first benchmarked sMEI detection methods, demonstrating advantages of long-read and MEI-targeted sequencing for ultra-rare events, and established an effective cross-platform integrative approach using a mixture of well-established cell lines. Haplotype phasing and donor-specific genome assemblies further refined sMEI calls by distinguishing germline and false signals in in silico tumor-normal mixtures. We also developed a source-tracing approach based on sequence variation within MEIs, expanding the catalog of active source elements beyond traditional transduction-based inference. Applying this framework to benchmark donor tissues, we detected rare somatic L1 insertions in all four tissue types examined, revealing structural and source diversity. Our work provides a foundational framework and biological insight into somatic retrotransposition in the human body.

papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of patient outcomes remains a critical challenge in oncology, in particular for childhood brain tumors, in which treatment decisions need to carefully balance risk of tumor recurrence and death against severe therapy-induced sequelae. Here, we developed MANTIS (methylation profiling and artificial neural networks for time-dependent individualized survival predictions), a precision artificial intelligence (AI) tool for medulloblastoma and ependymoma outcome prediction built on genome-wide DNA methylation array data from 2,786 patients. MANTIS generates individualized survival probabilities over a 10-year period and achieves concordance indices as high as 0.80 ± 0.07, significantly exceeding the predictive accuracy of current clinical indicators. Extending MANTIS to estimate individualized treatment effects identifies ~60% of patients with average-risk medulloblastoma without a significant survival disadvantage (P = 0.683) when treated with less intensive craniospinal irradiation doses, which is associated with improved neurocognitive outcomes. In conclusion, our study establishes a foundation for AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization in childhood brain tumors and offers a blueprint for similar initiatives in other cancer types.

papers.abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α-XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α-XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte-IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

papers.abstract: Relcobatinib (ELVN-001) is a next-generation, investigational, BCR::ABL1 active-site tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) with a unique P-loop folded-in binding mode designed to deliver best-in-class efficacy with an improved tolerability profile over that of other TKIs for the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). We demonstrate that relcobatinib has marked selectivity for BCR::ABL1, without inhibition of off-target kinases implicated in toxicities related to other TKIs. Relcobatinib exhibited greater selectivity than other active-site TKIs and demonstrated robust activity in vitro against native BCR::ABL1 and a broad range of clinically relevant TKI-resistant mutants. A BCR::ABL1 mouse xenograft model of human CML showed marked anti-tumor activity with relcobatinib as monotherapy, and, in combination with asciminib, showed further durable tumor regression, supporting the complementary mechanism of action between an active-site TKI and an allosteric inhibitor. Collectively, the preclinical profile of relcobatinib, marked by selective BCR::ABL1 targeting, supports its potential to improve efficacy and tolerability in the treatment of CML and other BCR::ABL1-driven malignancies, as monotherapy and in combination with an allosteric inhibitor.

papers.abstract: Stellate ganglion block (SGB), an interventional technique that modulates sympathetic activity, has been increasingly investigated beyond traditional pain management in cardiology, neuropsychiatry, and perioperative medicine. This narrative review examines the evolving role of SGB in contemporary anesthesia practice, emphasizing that its effects may extend beyond immediate peripheral sympatholysis to longer-lasting central neural modulation. Technically, ultrasound guidance facilitates precise needle placement and low-volume injection, with improved visualization of relevant anatomy and injectate spread. Dose-finding studies have refined local-anesthetic volume and concentration, whereas continuous blockade may extend sympatholysis in selected refractory conditions. Clinically, SGB has been used in selected pain conditions, including complex regional pain syndrome and herpes zoster-related pain, and has been investigated for non-pain indications such as post-traumatic stress disorder, refractory ventricular arrhythmias, and menopausal vasomotor symptoms. In perioperative settings, SGB has been evaluated for postoperative analgesia, modulation of inflammatory responses, and potential neuroprotective effects. Risk mitigation relies on real-time ultrasound visualization of the needle tip, adjacent vascular structures, and injectate spread, together with predefined management protocols for major complications. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized procedural parameters, and individualized treatment pathways to support the safe, precise, and evidence-based use of SGB across clinical settings.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension is commonly defined as MAP <65 mmHg. We evaluated whether cumulative exposure across multiple MAP thresholds provides additional mortality-associated information beyond this single threshold. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults having non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery using perioperative electronic health record data. Pressure-time burden and proportion of operative time were calculated across MAP thresholds from 50 to 150 mmHg. Decision-tree analysis using recursive partitioning sequentially grouped patients according to MAP exposure patterns associated with 30-day mortality. Discrimination of the multi-threshold blood-pressure-only model was compared with that of a model restricted to exposure below MAP 65 mmHg. Medication associations were exploratory. Among 388,407 patients, 30-day mortality was 1.49%. The multi-threshold model had greater validation discrimination than the MAP 65 mmHg model (AUROC, 0.619 vs. 0.591; ΔAUROC, 0.028; 95% CI, 0.025-0.037; p < 0.001), although the improvement was modest. Terminal exposure groups defined by complete combinations of MAP level and cumulative exposure had different observed mortality rates. Medication associations varied across groups. Observed 30-day mortality was generally higher with deeper hypotension and a greater proportion of operative time spent below MAP thresholds, although the relationship was not uniformly monotonic. Multi-threshold MAP exposure captured mortality-associated information not represented by exposure below MAP 65 mmHg alone, complementing this clinical threshold. The multi-threshold analysis identified groups with distinct pressure-time exposure patterns, providing a basis for hemodynamic profiling and investigation of hypotension-related outcomes. External validation is needed to assess the reproducibility and discrimination of these groups in other populations, followed by prospective studies to determine whether management informed by these patterns improves outcomes.

papers.abstract: Remifentanil infusion titrated to effect-site concentration (Ce) is commonly used to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia; nevertheless, the optimal Ce range remains unclear. We aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the existing evidence on the optimal Ce values of remifentanil for cough suppression during emergence. We performed a comprehensive literature search using PubMed®, Embase®, Web of Science™, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar on 27 February 2025. We included prospective studies that used the up-and-down method to estimate the effective concentrations of remifentanil in 50% of patients (EC50) and 95% of patients (EC95) for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia with tracheal intubation in adult patients. We excluded studies in children or patients undergoing cardiac surgery, as well as those that only compared predefined Ce targets of remifentanil to determine optimal dosing. We obtained pooled estimates using a random-effects model with inverse-variance method, and heterogeneity was quantified using the I2 statistic. We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies for nonrandomized comparative or single-arm studies. The primary outcome was EC50 estimated using the up-and-down method, with secondary outcomes including model-based EC50 and EC95 estimates. We included 22 prospective studies comprising 857 adult participants, and none were assessed as being at a high risk of bias or of low methodologic quality. Based on 28 groups and 653 participants across 17 studies, the pooled mean EC50 from the up-and-down method was 2.0 ng·mL-1 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8 to 2.3), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.5%). Based on 29 groups and 693 participants across 18 studies, the model-based EC50 was 1.9 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 1.6 to 2.1), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 96.1%). Based on 31 groups and 809 participants across 20 studies, the model-based EC95 was 2.7 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 2.5 to 3.0), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 99.5%). Subgroup analyses revealed higher mean EC50 values in male individuals (2.6 ng·mL-1) and the highest mean EC50 in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracic surgery (2.6 ng·mL-1). Using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework, the certainty of evidence was rated as very low for all outcomes. The identified EC50 and EC95 values of remifentanil for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults were 2.0 and 2.7 ng·mL-1, respectively. Patient sex and surgical type may influence the required Ce. Careful dose adjustment is recommended to avoid delayed awakening and hypoventilation, especially in cases requiring higher concentrations. papers.abstract: Inhaled anesthetic use contributes to environmental harm through release of potent greenhouse gases (GHG). Emissions can be reduced with the use of safe practice changes, including avoidance of high impact agents like desflurane and nitrous oxide, use of low fresh gas flows, and adoption of total intravenous and regional anesthesia when clinically appropriate. These evidence-based practices have been recommended for years, but actual practice changes have not been widely adopted. The Project SPRUCE (Saving our Planet by Reducing Carbon Emissions) consortium brought together twelve pediatric anesthesia groups into a partnership working to reduce GHG emissions from pediatric anesthesia care. The consortium implemented quality improvement strategies, including change management methods, to reduce GHG emissions from inhaled anesthetics by at least 50%. Change management and quality improvement strategies were utilized to disseminate strategies, implement emissions reduction techniques, and track emissions in pediatric anesthesia care. Specific interventions included education and socialization, practice constraints, and direct data feedback to clinical teams. The consortium facilitated adoption of practice changes among anesthesia groups, and sustained emissions reductions though shifts in culture. Greenhouse gas emissions from inhaled anesthesia decreased by 63% (range 43-91%) During the study period, the incidence of nitrous oxide use was reduced by 62.4%, and the average volume of nitrous oxide used per case decreased by 83.5%. Project SPRUCE prevented a total of 14,381 metric tons of excess carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) emissions from inhaled anesthetics. Collaborative action within our consortium supported widespread and significant reductions in harmful greenhouse gas emissions from pediatric anesthesia care through education and socialization, practice constraints, and direct data feedback to clinical teams.

papers.abstract: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade (NMB) is a routine component of general anaesthesia with important implications for recovery quality and peri-operative safety. Recent changes in the cost of sugammadex, together with its efficacy and adverse effect profile relative to neostigmine, may influence its broader clinical use. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of sugammadex compared with neostigmine in adult patients. Systematic review of randomised controlled trials with meta-analyses and trial sequential analyses. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grades of Recommendation, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. This is an update of a 2017 Cochrane review. Online databases were searched up to December 2025. Randomised trials enrolling adults receiving rocuronium or vecuronium for elective procedures and comparing sugammadex with neostigmine were included. The outcomes included NMB recovery time and risk of various adverse events. We included 165 trials with 19 124 participants. Risk of bias was generally unclear or high. NMB monitoring technique was reported in 113 trials, mostly acceleromyography. Time to reversal of NMB from second twitch to a train-of-four ratio more than 0.9 was shorter with sugammadex 2 mg kg-1 versus neostigmine 0.05 mg kg-1 (mean difference = -10.49 min (95% confidence interval, -11.90 to -9.08), GRADE: moderate). Sugammadex probably reduces the number of patients with at least one adverse event compared with neostigmine (risk ratio = 0.72 (95% confidence interval, 0.61 to 0.84), GRADE: moderate). When looking at specific adverse events, sugammadex probably reduces the risk of residual NMB, inadequate NMB reversal, desaturation, atelectasis, increased upper airway secretion, airway obstruction, bradycardia, dry mouth and urinary retention (GRADE: moderate). Sugammadex probably reverses NMB more rapidly and with fewer adverse events than neostigmine. Broader use of sugammadex has the potential to improve peri-operative outcomes.

papers.abstract: Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia is generally considered to follow an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with incomplete penetrance. In a recent study in the British Journal of Anaesthesia, Aboelsaod and colleagues integrate national epidemiological data, anaesthetic exposure histories, population genomics, contracture test phenotyping, and Bayesian modelling to estimate the prevalence of individuals capable of developing clinical malignant hyperthermia. Their findings support a threshold model in which variants contribute different degrees of biological liability, potentially modified by other genetic and environmental factors, whereas the probability of reacting during a triggering exposure seems relatively similar once an individual has crossed this threshold. The study also illustrates how combining complementary sources of imperfect evidence can improve risk estimation for rare, exposure-dependent disorders. Ultimately, malignant hyperthermia genetics needs to move beyond categorical variant classification towards variant-specific penetrance estimates that incorporate genetic background, ancestry, exposure history, and other determinants of clinical expression.

papers.abstract: We aimed to assess the public perception of who is responsible for anesthesia-related hospital care tasks in Japan and examine associated factors. We conducted a cross-sectional, nationwide, quota-based web survey of adults in Japan in July 2025. Of the 1,944 respondents who initiated the survey, 1,844 completed (94.9%) it, and 1,000 responses were analyzed after quota completion (ages 20-69 yr). The outcomes were attribution (yes/no) of four anesthesia-related hospital care tasks to anesthesiologists: intraoperative anesthesia, postoperative pain management, procedural sedation/analgesia (PSA), and labour neuraxial analgesia (LNA). For each outcome, we fitted multivariable logistic regression models adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, the Health Interest Scale (HIS), Communicative and Critical Health Literacy (CCHL), board-certified anesthesiologist density, information sources, and task-matched experience, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) control. Attribution was highest for intraoperative anesthesia (84.7%), followed by LNA (65.2%), PSA (37.4%), and postoperative pain management (13.5%). After FDR control, university education or higher was associated with greater attribution for intraoperative anesthesia (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.30 to 3.32), PSA (aOR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.15 to 2.30), and LNA (aOR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.30 to 2.55). Task-matched prior experience attributed to anesthesiologists was associated with higher attribution for intraoperative anesthesia (aOR, 3.75; 95% CI, 1.76 to 8.80) and PSA (aOR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.34 to 4.43). Fictional media was the only information-source factor that remained significant after FDR control (intraoperative anesthesia: aOR, 2.73; 95% CI, 1.79 to 4.25; PSA: aOR, 1.90; 95% CI, 1.42 to 2.56). No factor met the FDR threshold for postoperative pain management. HIS, CCHL, and anesthesiologist density showed no consistent adjusted associations. Public attribution of anesthesiologists' roles in Japan varied by task. Educational attainment, task-matched experience, and information sources were more consistently associated with attribution than general health traits or workforce context, supporting the value of role-explicit, task-specific communication strategies.

papers.abstract: Pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents remains an important cause of anaesthetic morbidity and mortality, and is important medicolegally. Rapid sequence induction is a multi-element technique designed to mitigate risk in those patients at increased risk of pulmonary aspiration during induction of general anaesthesia. We undertook a narrative review to summarise evidence and evidence gaps focusing on controversial aspects of rapid sequence induction. Despite widespread use of rapid sequence induction, many elements of the technique lack robust evidence and consensus. Nasogastric tubes can be used to reduce gastric content, but do not empty the stomach reliably. Correctly applied cricoid force obstructs the hypopharynx and has a limited impact on airway management, but incorrect application can cause clinically significant difficulties. Correct location of cricoid force may require ultrasound localisation of the cricoid cartilage. Applying the correct force, which varies with age and sex, is improved by education, practice and feedback. The use of videolaryngoscopy during rapid sequence induction is supported by evidence. The role of gastric ultrasound in determining anaesthetic technique is uncertain. Cardiovascular complications of rapid sequence induction are common, particularly in the patients who are critically ill, and modifications to the technique may reduce their frequency and severity. Effective use of airway rescue techniques may require removal of cricoid force. There is insufficient evidence for many of the elements of rapid sequence induction to determine whether they reduce patient harm or to state confidently that they do not. Controversies and evidence gaps should be acknowledged. Despite this, optimal use of rapid sequence induction requires a thorough knowledge of the subject, including areas of uncertainty to guide individualised risk assessment; clinical decision-making; and practical conduct of the technique.

papers.abstract: The Delphi methodology is a widely-used tool for achieving expert consensus in healthcare, particularly in areas where empirical evidence is limited or uncertain. Despite its structured design, the Delphi process remains vulnerable to implicit cognitive biases that may influence judgement and group decision-making. Such biases may inadvertently affect the quality of the consensus process, allow louder voices to influence outcomes, restrict inclusivity and undermine the validity, transparency and evidence-based nature of recommendations. We conducted a methodological review synthesising literature from cognitive psychology, behavioural science and methodological research on consensus development and Delphi processes. Using a concept-mapping approach, established cognitive biases were mapped to different stages of the Delphi process, including study design; panel selection; survey development; iterative scoring; and consensus interpretation. Ten cognitive biases were organised into four domains reflecting different levels of influence within consensus development: steering-group and design-level biases, panel composition and contextual biases, social influence and conformity biases; and individual cognitive heuristic biases. A conceptual framework was developed to systematically identify these biases within Delphi-based consensus studies. Examples illustrating how these biases may arise in healthcare Delphi processes are presented, alongside potential mitigation strategies. Recognition and mitigation of cognitive biases are essential for strengthening the methodological rigour and credibility of Delphi studies. Strategies to reduce bias include diversifying expert panels; using neutral language in survey statements; maintaining anonymity during voting; involving methodological expertise in Delphi design; and ensuring transparent iterative feedback. The framework needs prospective validation before its widespread use and may assist journal editors and peer reviewers in critically appraising Delphi studies and improving reporting standards in consensus research.

papers.abstract: Readmission after discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU) occurs globally at a rate of approximately 1-12% and is associated with adverse patient outcomes. Despite these findings, there is no internationally accepted tool to guide or standardize decisions regarding ICU discharge. In this scoping review, we aimed to evaluate the use of early warning scores (EWSs) measured at or around the time of ICU discharge as predictors of subsequent ICU readmission in adult and pediatric populations. With support from a medical librarian, we searched MEDLINE®, Embase®, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature from database inception to December 14, 2025. We included quantitative observational and interventional studies that evaluated any EWS (e.g., National EWS [NEWS]/NEWS2, Modified EWS [MEWS], Pediatric EWS [PEWS], Rothman Index, Risk Scoring Index, or related tools) at ICU discharge, immediately prior to transfer, or immediately upon ward admission and reported unplanned ICU readmission following transfer to a hospital ward. Unplanned ICU readmissions were defined as any unplanned return to an ICU after discharge to the ward. We excluded studies in which patients were discharged to locations other than a ward (e.g., home, long-term care) or that focused solely on interfacility transfer. Screening and data extraction were performed in duplicate using a standardized template, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The search identified 7,977 records, of which 4,824 remained after removal of duplicates. Of the articles, 58 underwent full-text review, and 20 studies met inclusion criteria. The studies were conducted across North America, Europe, and Asia and included both adult (n = 14) and pediatric (n = 6) populations. All were observational (retrospective or prospective) or pre-post intervention designs; no randomized controlled trials were identified. A range of tools were evaluated, including NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, PEWS, the Rothman Index, the Risk Scoring Index, and several machine-learning-based EWS models. Of the 20 studies, 17 reported a significant association between higher EWS values at or near ICU discharge and increased risk of unplanned ICU readmission, while three found no significant association. Across studies, readmission rates and EWS thresholds varied, and there was considerable heterogeneity in populations, settings, and outcome time frames. The risk of bias was generally low to moderate across QUADAS-2 domains, although several studies had high or unclear risk in key areas-most commonly patient selection and index test blinding-limiting causal inference. Most available studies report that higher EWS values at ICU discharge are associated with an increased likelihood of ICU readmission. Early warning scores may therefore serve as useful adjuncts to clinical judgement when assessing discharge readiness. Nevertheless, the current evidence base is limited by the absence of randomized or robust interventional trials, and substantial heterogeneity, which limits causal inference and the ability to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve outcomes. Further multicentre prospective studies are needed to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve patient outcomes, reduce readmissions, and optimize use of ICU resources.

papers.abstract: Pediatric adenotonsillectomy often causes preoperative anxiety, venous cannulation pain, and emergence agitation. Esketamine has multimodal properties, but the optimal oral dose for children is unknown. This study evaluated oral esketamine at 1, 2, and 3 mg/kg for perioperative comfort. In this randomized double-blind trial, 99 children (ASA I-II, 1-6 years) received oral 10% glucose (control, n = 26) or esketamine 1 mg/kg (EK1, n = 26), 2 mg/kg (EK2, n = 23), or 3 mg/kg (EK3, n = 24) 30 min before anesthesia. Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) and FLACC pain score at venous cannulation, and PAED score at 15 min after extubation. remifentanil use, postoperative FLACC (2-48 h), sleep quality, and adverse events. All esketamine doses improved sedation and analgesia at cannulation (overall p < 0.001), with largest effect at 3 mg/kg. Median RSS (IQR): control 1.00 (1.00-2.00); EK1 2.00 (1.75-3.00, p = 0.028); EK2 2.00 (1.00-3.00, p = 0.049); EK3 3.00 (2.00-3.37, p < 0.001). FLACC scores: control 6.00 (3.00-7.00); EK1 2.50 (1.00-4.00, p = 0.016); EK2 2.00 (0.00-4.00, p = 0.001); EK3 0.00 (0.00-1.75, p < 0.001). PAED score at 15 min was lower in EK2 than control (5.00 [2.00-10.00] vs. 10.00 [6.00-12.00], p = 0.048). Remifentanil consumption was reduced in EK3 (120.00 [80.00-159.50] vs. 240.00 [160.00-315.00] μg, p = 0.001). Postoperative pain at 2-6 h was lower in EK2 and EK3 (p < 0.05), persisting to 48 h in EK3 (p < 0.05). Sleep quality improved in EK3 at 24 h (p = 0.023) and 48 h (p = 0.032). Adverse events did not differ significantly. Preoperative oral esketamine (1-3 mg/kg) enhances perioperative comfort in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy. The 2 mg/kg dose offers the best balance of efficacy and safety, while 3 mg/kg provides superior analgesia and opioid sparing.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative cell salvage (CS) reduces allogeneic transfusion in cardiac surgery, but the washing process removes coagulation factors and platelets, raising hemostatic concerns. The dose-response relationship between CS volume and perioperative hemostatic changes remains poorly characterized. In this retrospective study of adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CS use, two cohorts with paired hemostatic measurements were identified: a routine coagulation cohort (primary analysis) and a viscoelastic cohort (exploratory analysis). Both cohorts were restricted to patients without coagulation-affecting blood products between measurements. Multivariable linear regression examined CS volume and absolute changes in each parameter, adjusted for surgical and patient characteristics and baseline values. In the routine coagulation cohort (N = 677; median CS 0.5 L, range 0.1-1.6 L), CS volume was not significantly associated with absolute changes in any parameter (all p ≥ 0.144). In the viscoelastic cohort (N = 50; median CS 0.8 L, range 0.2-3.7 L), CS volume was significantly associated with decreased functional fibrinogen clot strength (CFF MA: β = -3.31 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.53, -1.08; p = 0.004) and overall clot strength (CK MA: β = -2.93 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.73, -0.13; p = 0.041); after Holm correction for multiple testing, the CFF MA association remained significant (adjusted p = 0.031), whereas the CK MA association did not (adjusted p = 0.244). At observed reinfusion volumes, CS was not associated with changes in routine coagulation parameters, but in the exploratory viscoelastic cohort, higher CS volume was associated with lower functional fibrinogen clot strength. These findings highlight the potential value of viscoelastic monitoring when higher volumes are anticipated.

papers.abstract: High-risk patients need to carefully consider the risks and benefits of surgery. Shared decision-making is a collaborative process that enables patients and clinicians to share information and weigh up options and preferences. There is limited evidence about how best to organise the participation of the full range of healthcare professionals who can contribute to such decision-making processes. We conducted a Delphi study with a panel of experts to clarify how, and for what purposes, different healthcare professionals can contribute to shared decision-making with high-risk surgical patients. Consensus was reached on a conceptual model of multidisciplinary shared decision-making. The model recommends that interactions between patients, supported by family members and informal carers, and healthcare professionals are organised around five areas: options for management and treatment; patient values, goals, and preferences; comprehensive needs assessment; social context and home environment; and perioperative preparations. Experts agreed that achieving multidisciplinary shared decision-making in practice requires four key facilitators: early identification of patients with complex decision-making needs, availability of specialist expertise and support, sufficient time for discussion and decision-making, and coordination and information sharing between interactions. This model organises multidisciplinary involvement in high-risk surgical shared decision-making into five conceptually distinct and operationally interdependent areas. The model has the potential to inform practice and enhance opportunities for shared decision-making for high-risk surgical patients and their multidisciplinary teams.

papers.abstract: Posterior lumbar plexus block provides reliable anesthesia but is technically challenging and associated with risks related to deep paraspinal needle placement. Existing anterior approaches provide variable lumbar plexus coverage, and the anatomical pathways by which newer iliopsoas-based techniques reach individual plexus branches remain incompletely defined. This feasibility study evaluated whether an anterior inferior, trans-psoas injection targeting the posterior epimysium of the psoas muscle could provide a direct anterior pathway toward the lumbar plexus. A cadaveric dye study was performed on four GreenMBalmed cadaver hips. Under ultrasound guidance in the supine position, 30 mL of 0.1% methylene blue was injected in a caudal-to-cranial trajectory along the posterior epimysium of the psoas. Layered dissections assessed dye spread relative to the psoas, thoracolumbar fascia, and lumbar plexus nerves. Cranial and anterior fascial spread was observed in all four hips, with dye tracking anterior to the quadratus lumborum and extending toward the 12th rib and perinephric region. Dense staining of the lateral femoral cutaneous and iliohypogastric nerves was seen in all hips. The femoral nerve demonstrated predominantly moderate staining, while obturator nerve involvement was variable. Minimal intramuscular staining of the psoas was observed, suggesting preferential spread along fascial planes. Anterior inferior injection along the posterior epimysium of the psoas produced spread toward lumbar plexus regions in all four hips, in this limited cadaveric sample, suggesting this plane warrants further investigation. Clinical studies are needed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of this approach.

papers.abstract: Processed electroencephalography (pEEG) provides quantitative indices for monitoring anesthetic depth and is recommended in international guidelines. Prior meta-analyses have assessed EEG-guided anesthesia but none have evaluated available evidence stratified by pEEG technology. We performed a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in adults undergoing surgical, endoscopic, or dental procedures comparing pEEG-guided with non-pEEG-guided anesthesia. Primary outcomes were anesthetic drug use (TIVA and volatile agents) and postoperative delirium (POD ≤10 days). Secondary outcomes were extubation time, wake-up time, time to orientation, and post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay. Searches (PubMed Central, MEDLINE) were conducted on 11 April 2025; the protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251067170). Random-effects models produced standardized mean differences (SMD), mean differences (MD), and risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI). Eighty-seven RCTs (30,611 patients; 13,586 pEEG; 17,025 non-pEEG) were included. pEEG significantly reduced propofol use (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.10; p = 0.01) and volatile anesthetic use (SMD -1.27, 95% CI -1.88 to -0.66; p < 0.01). The risk of POD decreased by 27% (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.01). Efficiency outcomes favored pEEG: extubation time (MD -2.90 min, 95% CI -3.64 to -2.16; p < 0.01), wake-up time (MD -1.83 min, 95% CI -2.42 to -1.25; p < 0.01), time to orientation (MD -4.11 min, 95% CI -6.99 to -1.23; p < 0.01), and PACU length of stay (MD -2.81 min, 95% CI -4.66 to -0.96; p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses suggested benefits were most consistently observed for BIS; estimates for Entropy and SEDLine were less precise due to fewer studies. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes. Across 87 RCTs, pEEG-guided monitoring utilizing multiple device types improved perioperative efficiency and reduced POD compared with not using pEEG. Evidence is strongest for BIS; further well-reported trials are needed to delineate device-specific effects.

papers.abstract: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes. We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%. The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

papers.abstract: Chronic inferior vena cava (IVC) stenosis is an uncommon yet serious vascular complication that can significantly impact the success of liver transplantation. We report a case in which postreperfusion venovenous bypass (VVB) was used as a temporizing strategy to achieve hemodynamic stabilization in the setting of severe hepatic venous congestion caused by a fixed suprahepatic IVC obstruction. A 58-yr-old male with a history of orthotopic liver transplantation complicated by recurrent IVC stenosis and end-stage kidney disease underwent a simultaneous liver and kidney transplant. Intraoperatively, dense fibrosis was encountered proximal to the suprahepatic IVC, preventing resection of the stenotic segment. Although the liver graft was successfully implanted and reperfused, severe hepatic congestion and refractory hemodynamic instability developed. Venovenous bypass was initiated to augment venous return and stabilize systemic hemodynamics. The kidney transplant was aborted owing to the patient's instability. Postoperatively, the patient initially tolerated the procedure, however, he ultimately died in the intensive care unit. This case illustrates an unconventional postreperfusion application of VVB as a rescue measure for refractory hemodynamic instability. Given the presence of a fixed suprahepatic IVC obstruction, VVB only provided temporary hemodynamic support and did not result in graft recovery. This underscores the physiologic limitations of VVB in the presence of irreversible mechanical outflow obstruction and highlights the importance of early recognition and surgical adaptability in anatomically complex cases.

papers.abstract: Background: Many clinicians monitor the abductor digiti minimi (ADM) muscle during surgery using electromyography (EMG) for ease and consistency of electrode placement, while practice guidelines recommend monitoring of responses at the adductor pollicis (AP) muscle. This study compared the onset time of rocuronium neuromuscular block and the sugammadex-induced recovery time recorded simultaneously from the AP and ADM muscles. Methods: In 44 consenting patients undergoing general anesthesia, simultaneous EMG recording of ADM and AP muscles was performed. Right- and left-hand selection of monitored muscle (AP vs . ADM) was randomized, and patients’ handedness was recorded. The primary outcomes were the onset time of neuromuscular block (administration of rocuronium until train-of-four [TOF] count equal to 0), recovery time (time from sugammadex administration until TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9), and time to maximal recovery (sugammadex administration until TOF ratio equal to 1.0). Results: There were no significant differences between ADM and AP measurements in onset time, recovery to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9, or time to maximal recovery (TOF ratio equal to 1.0) between EMG responses recorded simultaneously from ADM and AP muscles. However, a difference in recovery times between ADM and AP existed, depending on which hand was monitored. When ADM was monitored on the right hand, the readings showed earlier recovery than AP, and the mean difference was 93 s (25% faster) and 105 s (20% faster) for time to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9 and time to TOF ratio equal to 1.0, respectively. There was no difference between the AP and ADM muscles when monitoring was performed on the left hand. Conclusions: The current study underscores the equivalency between ADM and AP muscles for routine neuromuscular monitoring during surgery. When monitoring the nondominant arm, the ADM and AP muscles have similar recoveries. In the dominant arm, the ADM muscle recovery is significantly faster than that of the AP muscle.

papers.abstract: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia ( 145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity. Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes). Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

papers.abstract: Fluid accumulation in surgical patients is associated with worse outcomes. Lung ultrasound (LUS) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading can assess congestion and thereby fluid tolerance. However, evidence regarding epidemiology, feasibility, and associations of reduced fluid tolerance with outcomes in surgical patients is lacking. This was a prospective single-centre observational cohort study in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery. LUS and VExUS were performed before surgery and daily for up to 5 days after surgery. Reduced fluid tolerance was defined as pulmonary congestion (B profile on LUS), systemic congestion (VExUS ≥2), or both. The primary outcome was the prevalence of reduced fluid tolerance. Secondary outcomes were feasibility of ultrasound assessments, Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 complications, and length of stay (LOS). Of the 200 participants included, 73 (37%) exhibited signs of reduced fluid tolerance, most commonly on postoperative day 4 (n=28; 14%). Reduced fluid tolerance was primarily driven by pulmonary congestion (n=69; 95%), whereas systemic congestion was rare. In most affected patients (47 of 73; 64%), reduced fluid tolerance was limited to 1 day. Of 1200 planned assessments, 146 (12%) were missing: 123 because participants declined, mostly owing to the burden of repeated assessments, and 23 (2%) because of incomplete views. Reduced fluid tolerance was associated with LOS of >7 days (odds ratio 3.29; 95% CI 1.03-10.70), but not with major postoperative complications (hazard ratio 1.18; 95% CI 0.49-2.86). Reduced fluid tolerance detected by ultrasound is common after major gastrointestinal surgery and associated with increased LOS. Ultrasound assessments were technically feasible, but repeated assessments were perceived as a burden by a substantial proportion of patients. NCT06166719 (principal investigator: A.P.J. Vlaar; first registered: 04-12-2023).

papers.abstract: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

papers.abstract: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) is commonly used in neurovascular surgery, in which intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring limits inhalation anaesthetic use. However, propofol causes hypotension, and prolonged infusions can delay emergence. Remimazolam, a benzodiazepine whose effects are reversible with flumazenil, has been associated with less intraoperative hypotension than propofol, but its use raises concerns about postoperative delirium (POD). We tested whether remimazolam-based TIVA is noninferior to propofol-based TIVA for POD. In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised noninferiority trial, adults undergoing elective intracranial aneurysm clipping, arteriovenous malformation resection, microvascular decompression, or superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass received remimazolam-based TIVA with flumazenil reversal at emergence, or propofol-based TIVA, both with remifentanil. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of POD within 5 days, assessed twice daily with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined delirium (3D-CAM). The prespecified noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points. Among 686 patients in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, POD occurred in 44 of 344 (12.8%) with remimazolam and 37 of 342 (10.8%) with propofol (risk difference, 1.97 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.85 to 6.80; one-sided P<0.001 for noninferiority); per-protocol results were consistent. Hypotensive burden below a mean arterial pressure threshold of 65 mm Hg was lower in the remimazolam group (median, 0 vs 7.5 mm Hg min; P<0.001), and tracheal extubation in the operating room was more frequent (85.2% vs 67.3%). Remimazolam-based TIVA met the prespecified criterion for noninferiority to propofol-based TIVA with respect to postoperative delirium after elective neurovascular surgery. Interpretation should take into account that the observed incidence of postoperative delirium was lower than anticipated when the noninferiority margin was defined. NCT06115031 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.abstract: Short-term peripheral nerve stimulation serves as a neuromodulation therapy that modulates neural activity to provide therapeutic benefit, particularly pain relief. This study investigated the effectiveness of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation as a minimally invasive approach for achieving pain relief. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception till September 10, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults comparing short-term peripheral nerve stimulation with sham stimulation or usual care. The primary outcome was the change in average pain intensity during the implantation period. Eight RCTs (543 participants) were included. Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in average pain intensity during the implantation period at 1-4 weeks (SMD = -0.48, 95% CI = -0.71 to -0.26, P < 0.0001) and 5-8 weeks (SMD = -0.96, 95% CI = -1.22 to -0.70, P < 0.0001), but no significant result after electrode removal. For worst pain intensity, the intervention group showed a greater reduction than the control group at all time periods except 1-4 weeks after EOT. Improvements in pain interference were delayed, becoming significant at 5-8 weeks during the implantation period (MD = -1.34, 95% CI = -1.86 to -0.82, P < 0.00001) and ≥8 weeks after the end of treatment (MD = -1.09, 95%CI = -1.69 to -0.50, P = 0.0003). Subgroup analyses showed improvements in postoperative pain. The usual care-controlled subgroup showed more pronounced and sustained benefits than the sham-controlled subgroup, and the chronic pain subgroup also showed more pronounced and sustained benefits compared to the acute/subacute pain subgroup. This meta-analysis provided preliminary evidence that short-term peripheral nerve stimulation may relieve pain during the implantation period, but not all outcomes suggest sustained improvements after electrode removal. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Non‐pharmacological interventions are essential to reduce procedural anxiety in pediatric care. Fidget and sensory toys are widely used for distraction and self‐regulation, yet evidence on their effectiveness remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the evidence on fidget and sensory toys across general pediatric settings, with a focus on perioperative outcomes—such as anxiety, distress, and pain—to highlight relevant gaps in care. Methods This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA‐ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL, complemented by trial registries, gray literature, citation tracking, and reference screening. Studies involving children (0–18 years) evaluating fidget or sensory toys in any setting were eligible. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Findings Fifteen studies published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Fidget spinners were the most frequently investigated device ( n = 9), followed by stress balls ( n = 3). Studies were conducted in educational ( n = 8) and healthcare settings ( n = 7). Educational studies generally reported limited or no benefits for attention, engagement, behavior, or academic performance. In contrast, healthcare studies generally suggested reductions in anxiety, pain, fear, and procedural distress, although findings were heterogeneous, and outcome measures varied substantially. Conclusions Current evidence does not support the routine use of fidget toys to improve attention or academic performance in educational settings. Evidence from healthcare and procedural settings suggests that fidget and sensory toys may be feasible distraction tools for selected pediatric patients, but evidence is insufficient to support routine perioperative use. Further high‐quality randomized controlled trials are needed to establish standardized intervention protocols and identify the pediatric populations and clinical settings most likely to benefit.

papers.abstract: Late motor responses, including F-waves and H-reflexes, are commonly recorded during electrophysiological diagnostic evaluation in awake patients. Although these responses could offer added value during intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring, their use has not yet been widely adopted. This systematic review aims to assess current knowledge on how anesthetic and surgical factors influence the recording and monitoring of spinal late responses during surgery. The authors searched PubMed and EMBASE for relevant articles on studies of late response recording. Studies were considered eligible if the influence of one or more of the following parameters on late responses were assessed: (1) ventilation and metabolic parameters, (2) volatile agents, (3) intravenous agents, (4) neuromuscular blocking agents, (5) epidural or intrathecal agents, or (6) surgical factors. The QUADAS-2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias and concerns regarding applicability. Sixty-two studies were included. Respiratory conditions like hypercapnia reduced H-reflex amplitude, whereas hyperoxia and intermittent hypoxia had limited impact. Volatile agents, including isoflurane, sevoflurane, and nitrous oxide decreased late response amplitudes, with dose-dependent effects. Most intravenous anesthetics, particularly propofol, reduced H-reflex amplitude and F-wave persistence in a dose-dependent manner. Conversely, ketamine was found to increase H-reflex amplitude. During spinal and vascular surgeries, H-reflex monitoring proved feasible and provided valuable supplementary data to the conventional motor evoked potential (MEP) and somatosensory evoked potential (SSEP) modalities. This systematic review demonstrates that H-reflexes and F-waves are significantly influenced by anesthetic factors. The reviewed studies indicate that intravenous and volatile anesthetics significantly affect late responses, by reducing H-reflex and F-wave amplitudes, whereas latencies appear unaffected. The methodological quality varied significantly across the included studies and affects the interpretation of their conclusions. These findings support the potential integration of late response monitoring into intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM) protocols, provided that anesthetic management and surgical context are carefully considered.

papers.abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain after thoracoscopic surgery remains common. We investigated whether perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion would reduce chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection. In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. Esketamine was administered as a 0.1 mg kg-1 bolus at induction, followed by continuous intraoperative infusion (0.1 mg kg-1 h-1) and postoperative infusion (0.015 mg kg-1 h-1) for 48 h. The primary outcome was chronic pain at 3 months, defined as persistent pain with a numeric rating scale score ≥1 during coughing in the surgical region. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, supplemental analgesics use, recovery of bowel function, in-hospital adverse events, and esketamine-related side-effects. We analysed 873 patients (median age, 55 yr; 63% female). The incidence of 3 month chronic pain was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (14.7% vs 21.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.90; P=0.013). A reduction was also observed when using a post hoc outcome definition of a numeric rating scale pain score ≥3 during coughing at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.19-0.84; P=0.015). Esketamine also reduced overall pain scores at rest and during coughing within the first 48 h, and decreased supplemental analgesic requirements within 48 h and 3 months. Perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion significantly reduced 3 month chronic pain after thoracoscopic lung resection without increasing adverse effects. ChiCTR2000040012. This trial was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Identifier: ChiCTR2000040012; principal investigator: Fu-hai Ji; dated November 18, 2020; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=62319).

papers.abstract: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability. To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines. A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel. Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied. This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

papers.abstract: State Entropy (SE) and Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) parameters aim to optimise anaesthetic depth and intraoperative opioid administration, but their impact on postoperative complications remains unclear. Insufficient training and limited decision support may contribute to inconsistent findings. Thus, we evaluated whether tailored training to improve SE and SPI compliance reduced major postoperative complications. Adult inpatients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk noncardiac surgery were included in this prospective single-centre before-after study in France. The educational intervention and outcomes were based on the Kirkpatrick framework. All anaesthesia providers were invited to participate voluntarily in lectures and bedside training on SE and SPI monitoring. Training impact was assessed using a composite of major postoperative complications within 28 days as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included changes in monitoring practices. Among 1,623 eligible patients, 1,025 were included over a 13-month period (517 before and 508 after training). Of 202 eligible providers, 91 participated in the one-month training programme (45%). After training, simultaneous SE and SPI sensor use increased from 26% to 42% (P < 0.001), and combined SE-SPI compliance increased from 23% to 39% (P < 0.001). Major postoperative complications occurred in 66/517 patients (13%) before and 71/508 patients (14%) after training (P = 0.6). Multivariable and propensity score analyses showed no significant association between the intervention and the primary outcome. This training did not reduce the incidence of major postoperative complications, despite improvements in intraoperative monitoring practices. Future educational strategies should strengthen provider engagement and reinforcement to translate improved monitoring practices into clinical benefit. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06111248.

papers.abstract: To compare ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block with transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block on recovery quality 24 h after septorhinoplasty. Prospective, randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial. Tertiary training hospital; operating room and postoperative ward. Ninety adults aged 18 to 65 years, ASA physical status I or II, undergoing elective septorhinoplasty; 89 were analyzed. After induction of general anesthesia, patients received bilateral transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPG group) or bilateral ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block (IO group), 2 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine per side. Surgical infiltration and multimodal analgesia were identical in both groups. The primary outcome was the total Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 h. Secondary outcomes were QoR-15 domains, visual analog scale pain scores, rescue morphine, nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption, emergence agitation, edema, ecchymosis and recovery room stay. Total QoR-15 at 24 h was higher in the IO group (129.1 ± 9.4 versus 116.6 ± 11.7; mean difference 12.5 points, 95% CI 8.01 to 17.01; P = 0.001), above the prespecified minimal clinically important difference of 8. More IO patients crossed the acceptable symptom state threshold of 118 (86.4% versus 35.6%; P < 0.001). Pain scores were lower at every time point and fewer IO patients needed rescue analgesia (11.4% versus 53.3%; P = 0.001). Nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption and recovery room stay did not differ. Infraorbital nerve block gave better 24 h patient-reported recovery than sphenopalatine ganglion block after septorhinoplasty. Secondary findings are hypothesis-generating.
